papers.title: Perceptual proximity and semantic chunk tightness in Chinese remote association: behavioral and event-related potential findings.
papers.abstract: Remote association requires solvers to overcome salient but misleading cue relations, yet it remains unclear how perceptual organization and semantic experience jointly constrain early problem representations. This event-related potential (ERP) study manipulated semantic chunk tightness (no chunk, low-frequency chunk, and high-frequency chunk) and perceptual proximity in a Chinese character remote association task. Twenty-seven undergraduates completed the task while electroencephalography was recorded. High-frequency semantic chunks reduced solution accuracy relative to no-chunk trials. Neither the behavioral main effect of perceptual proximity nor its interaction with semantic chunk tightness was significant; response time showed no significant effects. Neither semantic chunk tightness nor proximity showed a significant main effect on P200, N400, or late positive component amplitudes. Exploratory follow-up comparisons of higher-order interactions involving scalp region yielded nominal proximity-related amplitude differences in selected semantic conditions and time windows. The behavioral findings support an effect of high-frequency semantic chunking on solution accuracy but do not support an effect of proximity or a proximity-by-chunking interaction on performance. The ERP patterns are exploratory and require confirmation with appropriate control of multiple comparisons; their implications for successful problem solving remain uncertain.

papers.title: Adolescent Obesity and Long-Term All-Cause and Cardiovascular Mortality Independent of 24-Hour Movement Behaviors.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to determine the associations between adolescent adiposity and long-term all-cause and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality and to evaluate whether adherence to recommended 24-hour movement behaviors modifies these associations. This was a prospective population-based cohort study using data from Wave I (1994-1995) of the Add Health study, with mortality follow-up through 2021. The analytic sample included 16,758 adolescents. Adolescent adiposity was assessed using age- and sex-standardized body mass index z-score (continuous, per 1-standard deviation increase) and obesity status. Adherence to 24-hour movement behavior recommendations was assessed via self-report and categorized individually and jointly. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models accounting for the Add Health complex sampling design. Among 16,758 adolescents (survey-weighted mean age, 16.0 years), 249 all-cause deaths, including 49 CVD deaths, occurred during follow-up. Each 1-standard deviation increase in adolescent body mass index z-score was associated with higher all-cause mortality (HR = 1.50; 95% CI, 1.25-1.79) and CVD mortality (HR = 2.01; 95% CI, 1.24-3.26). Adolescent obesity was also associated with higher all-cause (HR = 1.82; 95% CI, 1.18-2.78) and CVD mortality (HR = 4.41; 95% CI, 1.04-18.74). In joint models (reference: nonobese adolescents meeting ≥ 2 movement recommendations), adolescents with obesity meeting 0-1 recommendation had higher all-cause mortality (HR = 1.47; 95% CI, 1.02-1.98), whereas those with obesity meeting ≥ 2 recommendations did not show a significantly higher risk (HR = 1.16; 95% CI, 0.65-2.07). Adolescent obesity was associated with higher long-term mortality, while adherence to multiple healthy movement behaviors may attenuate excess all-cause mortality among adolescents with obesity.
papers.journal: The Journal of adolescent health : official publication of the Society for Adolescent Medicine

papers.title: Multi-Sensory Stimulation Therapy for Sleep and Cognitive Outcomes in Post-Stroke Sleep Disorders: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Post-stroke sleep disorders can interfere with rehabilitation and may adversely affect cognitive function and quality of life. This study evaluated multi-sensory stimulation therapy (MSST) in patients with post-stroke sleep disorders (PSSD). In this prospective, assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial, 84 patients with ischemic stroke and PSSD were randomly assigned to MSST plus routine care or routine care alone. MSST consisted of a structured 4-week program incorporating visual-cognitive, tactile, olfactory, and gustatory stimulation. Sleep quality was assessed using the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), cognitive function using the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) Cognitive Function measure, and health-related quality of life using the EQ-5D-5L. Outcomes were assessed at baseline, after the 4-week intervention, and at the 3-month follow-up. Seventy-eight participants completed the study and were included in the analysis. ISI-based clinical response rates did not differ significantly between groups at either post-intervention assessment. Continuous ISI scores and changes from baseline also showed no significant between-group differences. PROMIS analyses showed significant group × time interactions for memory, executive function, and total cognitive-function score, but not for information processing or attention. Quality-of-life differences were domain-specific and did not demonstrate a consistent overall benefit. These findings indicate that the effects of MSST on sleep and secondary outcomes were mixed and should be interpreted cautiously. Larger multicenter randomized controlled trials incorporating objective sleep and cognitive measures, attention-matched controls, longer follow-up, and intention-to-treat analyses are needed to confirm these findings.

papers.title: Maternal sequelae after SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy: results from the Post-CRONOS project.
papers.abstract: Long-COVID and post-COVID syndrome (PCS) are increasingly recognized as relevant complications following SARS-CoV-2 infection, yet data on long-term maternal outcomes after infection during pregnancy remain scarce. Given the unique physiological and psychosocial demands of the postpartum period, persistent symptoms may represent a substantial underrecognized burden. This retrospective cohort study was conducted within the Post-CRONOS project, an extension of the German CRONOS registry. Women with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy were invited to participate in a web-based survey assessing symptoms and quality of life (QoL) up to 12 months postpartum. PCS was defined as symptoms lasting more than 12 weeks after acute infection. A total of 398 women were included. Overall, 66.1 % reported symptoms persisting beyond 12 weeks, and 58.8 % reported at least one ongoing symptom at follow-up. Most frequent symptoms were fatigue (43.4 %), cognitive impairment (33.0 %), sleep disturbances (28.2 %), headache (26.4 %), and anxiety (23.2 %). Women with persistent symptoms showed significantly reduced QoL (p<0.001). Higher disease severity, lack of vaccination, and earlier infection during pregnancy were associated with an increased risk of PCS. The prevalence of persistent symptoms was consistent with findings from a pilot phase, supporting the robustness of the results. Persistent symptoms after SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy are highly prevalent. Although some symptoms overlap with physiological changes in the postpartum period, the high prevalence and prolonged persistence observed suggest that PCS contributes relevantly to maternal morbidity. These findings underscore the need for structured postpartum follow-up and multidisciplinary care strategies to address PCS in this population.

papers.title: An Experimental Framework for Multimodal Upper-Limb Reach-and-Grasp Assessment.
papers.abstract: Objective and quantitative evaluation of upper-limb motor function remains challenging, as conventional clinical tests and many digital assessment tools primarily focus on isolated behavioral outcomes. A comprehensive characterization of motor function requires the integration of complementary measures capturing movement execution, muscle activation, and cortical activity. Here, we present reaching and grasping for upper-limb assessment (ReGULA), a standardized multimodal framework for quantifying upper-limb motor abilities during functional reach-and-grasp-transport tasks, together with guided reaching and repositioning adjustable assessment platform (GRRAASP), a modular and sensorized device designed to support the ReGULA implementation. Conceived around the key principles of modularity, standardization, and synchronization, GRRAASP provides a highly versatile tool for research in motor control and in clinical assessment. It enables the synchronized acquisition of behavioral, kinematic, electromyographic (EMG), and electroencephalographic (EEG) signals across different movement phases, while its open architecture allows for the integration of any complementary acquisition modality. Here, we detail the step-by-step construction of the GRRAASP platform, the implementation of the ReGULA protocol, and the extraction of quantitative performance indicators covering multiple motor abilities. To demonstrate the GRRAASP application, it was tested in 30 healthy participants, providing population-level reference distributions of neurophysiological and kinematics metrics, and illustrating its ability to characterize individual differences in motor strategies. ReGULA and GRRAASP provide a flexible and reproducible research framework for multimodal upper-limb motor assessment, supporting the investigation of neuromechanical control, compensatory strategies, and motor recovery.

papers.title: Explainable Multimodal Machine Learning Estimates Weekly Countermovement Jump Readiness in Collegiate Badminton Players.
papers.abstract: Longitudinal athlete monitoring generates repeated information on training exposure, physiological status, sleep, and perceived recovery, but the extent to which these domains jointly estimate short-term neuromuscular readiness remains uncertain. This prospective longitudinal study evaluated an explainable multimodal machine-learning framework for estimating weekly countermovement-jump (CMJ) change in collegiate badminton players. Ninety-six athletes completed a 12-week protocol comprising familiarization, baseline assessment, and 10 analytic monitoring weeks, yielding 960 athlete-week observations. Eight primary predictors represented autonomic physiology, sleep, external and internal training load, and subjective recovery and stress. The Short Recovery and Stress Scale (SRSS) was completed immediately before warm-up, whereas all other dynamic predictors summarized the preceding 168 h. Weekly CMJ percentage change from individual baseline was the target. Elastic Net, Random Forest, and XGBoost were evaluated using nested athlete-grouped cross-validation, with all observations from each held-out athlete excluded from corresponding model development. The Integrated XGBoost model achieved a mean outer-fold R2 of 0.446 ± 0.068, root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.680 ± 0.128 percentage points, and mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.320 ± 0.096 percentage points; pooled out-of-fold R2 was 0.448 (95% confidence interval, 0.391-0.502). The SRSS-only model was the strongest single-domain model (R2 = 0.405 ± 0.068), corresponding to an absolute R2 gain of 0.041 with multimodal integration. Held-out SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) ranked SRSS Recovery, SRSS Stress, weekly session-RPE load, and lnRMSSD as the largest contributors to Integrated-model predictions. These results support moderate same-day pre-performance readiness estimation from longitudinal monitoring data while preserving athlete-level separation between model development and evaluation. SHAP contributions reflect predictive associations and should not be interpreted as causal effects or as prospective forecasts beyond the assessment day.

papers.title: Long-Term Memory in the Human Information-Processing System: An Organizational Reinterpretation.
papers.abstract: Long-term memory is a fundamental component of human cognition and has traditionally been investigated in relation to the encoding, consolidation, storage, and retrieval of information. Established accounts also recognize the contribution of prior knowledge to ongoing perception and cognition. Building on these accounts, the present review reinterprets the organizational role of long-term memory within the integrated human information-processing system, emphasizing the distinction between the memory system and the accumulated knowledge structures it represents. The review develops an organizational interpretation in which long-term memory is conceptualized as a continuously participating component that interacts dynamically with the other components of the information-processing architecture, while modulatory components of information processing influence these interactions according to their distinct functional roles. A central feature of this framework is the explicit distinction between long-term memory as a component of the information-processing architecture and accumulated knowledge structures as the cognitive contents represented within that component. This distinction provides a unified organizational framework for understanding how previously acquired knowledge continuously contributes to the interpretation, organization, integration, and adaptive modification of ongoing cognitive activity. To evaluate this perspective, the review integrates evidence from cognitive psychology, neuropsychology, lesion studies, functional neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and contemporary network neuroscience. Rather than proposing a new cognitive architecture, it reinterprets established empirical findings within a broader organizational framework that emphasizes the continuous participation of long-term memory throughout cognition. The review concludes by considering the theoretical, neuropsychological, and interdisciplinary implications of this organizational perspective for understanding human cognition.

papers.title: Urgent Pediatric Seizure Code: Results and limitations after its 1st year of implementation.
papers.abstract: To evaluate the appropriateness of activations of the Urgent Pediatric Seizure Code (UPSC) in 2 pediatric emergency departments after its 1st year of implementation and analyze compliance with its main quality indicators. We conducted a bicenter, descriptive, retrospective study including patients < 16 years in whom the UPSC was activated between November 2023 and November 2024. Of the 215 UPSC activations, 176 episodes (81.9%) were appropriately activated (recommended standard, 85%). The most common reason for activation was seizure clusters, which influenced compliance with several indicators. The indicator for early treatment with an antiseizure drug showed a compliance rate of 10.0%, while the diagnostic indicator [performance of video electroencephalogram (vEEG) within the first 24 hours] reached 95.5%. Overall, 33.0% of patients were discharged early within less than 24 hours. After 1 year of UPSC implementation, most activations in pediatric patients were appropriate. Early vEEG performance was excellent, whereas early treatment and discharge within 24 hours were insufficient. These findings highlight the need to adapt the protocol to the pediatric setting.
papers.journal: Emergencias : revista de la Sociedad Espanola de Medicina de Emergencias

papers.title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Upper Aerodigestive Complications after Single- and Multilevel ACDF: A National Propensity-Matched Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Study DesignRetrospective Cohort Study.ObjectivesObstructive sleep apnea (OSA) involves pharyngeal neuromuscular dysfunction in the same anatomic region retracted during anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF). Using a national claims database, this study evaluated the association between OSA and postoperative upper aerodigestive complications following single and multilevel ACDF and explored postoperative outcomes according to preoperative continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP)-related coding among patients with OSA.MethodsA retrospective cohort study was performed using the PearlDiver Mariner database. Patients undergoing ACDF were stratified by OSA status and propensity matched on age, sex, Elixhauser Comorbidity Index, BMI, and tobacco use. A secondary analysis compared patients with and without preoperative CPAP-related coding. Upper aerodigestive outcomes were assessed within 2 years, surgical outcomes within 1 year, and postoperative opioid utilization within 180 days. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors, with an additional OSA-by-surgical extent interaction analysis performed in the overall ACDF cohort.ResultsSingle-level cohorts included 6,022 matched pairs; multilevel cohorts included 66,779 matched pairs. OSA was not independently associated with upper aerodigestive complications in the original single-level analysis (OR 1.06; 95% CI 0.97-1.17; p=0.20) but was associated with modestly higher adjusted odds in the multilevel cohort (OR 1.12; 95% CI 1.09-1.15; p<0.001). No significant OSA-by-surgical extent interaction was detected in the overall ACDF cohort (ratio of ORs 0.96; 95% CI 0.88-1.04; p=0.314). In the multilevel cohort, upper aerodigestive complications occurred in 11.92% of patients with OSA and 11.11% of patients without OSA, corresponding to an absolute risk difference of 0.80 percentage points and an unadjusted number needed to harm of approximately 125. OSA was not associated with increased rates of wound infection, hematoma, implant removal, or reoperation in either cohort. Among patients with OSA undergoing multilevel ACDF, preoperative CPAP-related coding was associated with lower adjusted odds of upper aerodigestive complications (OR 0.91; 95% CI 0.87-0.95; p<0.001).ConclusionsIn stratum-specific analyses, OSA was associated with a statistically significant but clinically modest increase in upper aerodigestive complications after multilevel ACDF, whereas no statistically significant association was observed in the original single-level analysis. However, no statistically significant OSA-by-surgical extent interaction was detected, and these findings should not be interpreted as evidence that surgical extent modifies the OSA association. Preoperative CPAP-related coding was associated with lower adjusted odds of upper aerodigestive complications in the multilevel cohort; however, this exploratory claims-based association should not be interpreted as evidence of a protective treatment effect.

papers.title: Genetic variation and subjective sleep domains in fibromyalgia: exploratory associations in serotonergic and opioidergic systems.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbance is a key feature of fibromyalgia (FM) and is closely intertwined with pain burden and daytime impairment. Functional variants in serotonergic and opioidergic systems have been linked to pain processing and depressive symptoms, but it remains unclear whether they are also associated with overall subjective sleep quality and specific domains of subjective sleep disturbance in FM. In this cross-sectional study, data from a pooled cohort of 253 women with FM were analysed. Valid genotype data were available for 237-242 participants across the analysed polymorphisms, whereas the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) component data varied across outcomes. Pain burden was assessed using the SF-36 Bodily Pain subscale and depressive symptoms using the depression subscale of the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale. Participants were genotyped for HTR1A (rs6295), SLC6A4 (triallelic 5-HTTLPR/rs25531), and OPRM1 (rs1799971). Regression models examined associations between the candidate polymorphisms and the global PSQI score and individual PSQI component scores, adjusting for pain burden and depressive symptoms. Exploratory pairwise gene-gene interactions were also examined. Pain burden showed the strongest and most consistent associations across subjective sleep domains. Beyond these covariates, SLC6A4 (5-HTTLPR/rs25531) was associated with daytime dysfunction, and OPRM1 with the PSQI sleep medication component, whereas no robust associations were observed for HTR1A across PSQI components. Effect sizes were small, and the component-level genetic findings should be regarded as exploratory. No statistically significant genetic associations were identified with the global PSQI score, either before or after adjustment for multiple testing. In FM, subjective sleep disturbance was more strongly associated with pain burden than with the examined candidate polymorphisms. The observed genetic associations were limited, domain-specific, and exploratory, suggesting that any contribution of the examined variants to subjective sleep disturbance is likely modest.

papers.title: Association Between Adherence to 24-h Movement Guidelines and Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Fatty Liver Disease in American Adults: NHANES 2017-2020.
papers.abstract: Physical activity (PA), sedentary behavior (SB), and sleep are each associated with metabolic health, but their combined associations with metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) and hepatic fibrosis remain unclear. We examined associations of recommendation counts and mutually exclusive movement-behavior patterns with prevalent MAFLD and fibrosis phenotypes. This cross-sectional analysis included 7678 adults from National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2017-March 2020. Movement behaviors were classified using three study-defined thresholds informed by the Canadian adult guidelines, and MAFLD required hepatic steatosis (controlled attenuation parameter [CAP] ≥ 285 dB/m) and qualifying metabolic criteria. We used multivariable logistic regression and conducted subgroup and sensitivity analyses. Complete-case models additionally adjusted for the Healthy Eating Index-2015 (HEI-2015), total energy intake, and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) score; sensitivity analyses used the PHQ-9 score excluding the sleep item and incorporated the NHANES survey design. Among single-recommendation patterns, meeting only the SB recommendation (≤ 8 h/day) was associated with lower odds of prevalent MAFLD (odds ratio [OR]: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.46-0.83). Compared with meeting no recommendations, meeting all three recommendations was associated with the lowest odds (OR: 0.53, 95% CI: 0.40-0.70); the PA plus SB pattern showed a similar inverse association (OR: 0.54, 95% CI: 0.41-0.72). In the complete-case analysis (n = 6841), the estimate for meeting all three recommendations remained inverse after additional adjustment for HEI-2015, total energy intake, and PHQ-9 (OR: 0.48, 95% CI: 0.36-0.65). The inverse association persisted when the PHQ-9 sleep item was excluded and when the NHANES survey design was incorporated. In this cross-sectional NHANES sample, meeting only the SB recommendation was associated with lower odds of prevalent MAFLD. Meeting both PA and SB recommendations was also inversely associated with MAFLD. These findings do not establish that changing these behaviors prevents MAFLD.

papers.title: Harnessing multi-assay new approach methodologies for cardiotoxicity screening of complex botanical mixtures.
papers.abstract: Botanicals are widely used, yet pre-market cardiotoxicity evaluation remains limited despite reports of cardiovascular adverse events. The Botanical Safety Consortium (BSC) evaluated human-relevant new approach methodologies (NAMs) for screening cardiotoxic effects of botanical extracts. To evaluate the suitability of a battery of NAM-based assays for botanicals, using botanical extracts with well-reported evidence of cardiotoxicity, or lack thereof. Botanical extracts were evaluated using human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocyte (hiPSC-CM) assays measuring contractility, electro-physiology, calcium handling, and mitochondrial function. Six extracts were selected: four known cardiotoxicants (aconite, oleander, ephedra, and yohimbe) and two with low-expected cardiotoxicity (Asian ginseng and milk thistle). Known cardiotoxic botanical extracts produced pronounced, concentration-dependent effects across assays. Aconite extract increased beat rate and altered electrophysiological and calcium handling parameters. Oleander extract caused contractile and electrophysiological disturbances, including cessation of beating at higher concentrations. Ephedra extract increased beat rate and altered electrophysiological endpoints. Yohimbe extract produced concentration-dependent effects on calcium transient duration and electrophysiological activity. In contrast, Asian ginseng and milk thistle extracts produced minimal effects across endpoints. Mitochondrial respiration assays demonstrated reduced respiratory capacity following exposure to aconite, oleander, and ephedra extracts. Overall, the assays were able to identify botanical extracts with known cardiotoxic liabilities and generally showed fewer responses in those with limited evidence of cardiotoxicity. Multiple NAMs were able to identify cardiotoxicity-associated responses in botanical extracts. These findings support development of fit-for-purpose NAM toolkits for botanical safety assessment which can contribute to reducing animal testing.
keywords: Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs)

papers.title: Application of Visible/near-Infrared Spectroscopy and Hyperspectral Imaging with Machine Learning for High-Throughput Phenotyping of Pesticide and Herbicide Stressed Plants.
papers.abstract: Rapid, accurate, and nondestructive detection of pesticide and herbicide stress in plants is crucial for agrochemical research, precision agriculture, and food safety. Conventional analytical methods are often time-consuming, labor-intensive, and destructive, limiting high-throughput use. Visible/near-infrared (VIS/NIR) spectroscopy and hyperspectral imaging (HSI) are powerful alternatives, capturing stress-induced biochemical, physiological, spectral, and spatial changes for comprehensive plant phenotyping. Combined with drones, ground robots, conveyors, and controlled facilities, they support high-throughput applications, while advanced machine intelligence improves data analysis accuracy and efficiency. This review summarizes recent progress in VIS/NIR spectroscopy and HSI for phenotyping pesticide- and herbicide-stressed plants, linking physiological and biochemical changes to wavelength-dependent spectral responses and spatial patterns. It also reviews representative preprocessing methods, feature selection, vegetation indices, traditional machine learning, deep learning, and integrated high-throughput phenotyping platforms. Current limitations include insufficient model transferability across species and growth stages, environmental variability, scarce standardized datasets, inconsistent evaluation protocols, limited interpretability, and field deployment difficulties in real-world fields. Future research should emphasize explainable artificial intelligence, model reliability, transfer learning, domain adaptation, calibration transfer, multi-source data fusion, and automated platforms to enable robust, scalable, and reliable field-deployable stress detection in modern precision agriculture.

papers.title: Sleep-Wake Transitions Reveal Distinct Sex-, Race-, Age-, and Sleep State-Specific Electrocardiographic Autonomic Dynamics in Community Adults.
papers.abstract: Sleep comprises one-third of our lives. Autonomic function during sleep is vital for health, yet fundamental population-level information on autonomic changes during sleep-wake transitions remain incompletely characterized. Demographic factors may shape these dynamics in ways not captured during daytime testing. We hypothesized that autonomic changes during sleep-wake transitions differ by demographic group independent of established cardiovascular risk factors. We analyzed 5589 consecutive adults who were in sinus rhythm during overnight home polysomnography in the Sleep Heart Health Study. The ratio of ECG-derived sympathetic-to-parasympathetic (sympathovagal) modulation and EntropyXRR, a nonlinear dynamic measure, was evaluated across 6 sleep-wake stages. Marginal means were estimated for age, sex, and race or ethnicity using mixed-effects models adjusted for cardiovascular risk factors. Interaction terms were used to quantify demographic differences in state-specific autonomic responses. Participants were (median [interquartile range]) 63 [55-72] years old, 53% female, and 15% non-White (9% Black, 6% other races or ethnicities including Hispanic, Asian, and Pacific Islander). Age, sex and race were strongly associated with autonomic changes, but not EntropyXRR, during sleep state transitions independent of cardiovascular risk factors. Sympathovagal modulation: (1) was lowest in female, non-White, and oldest quartile adults; (2) increased transiently during sleep onset for all groups except non-White; and (3) exhibited the largest changes associated with greatest demographic disparities during final morning awakening from sleep. These were driven primarily by changes in vagal modulation. Sleep-wake transitions reveal robust age-, sex-, and race-specific autonomic signatures not apparent during steady-state sleep. This novel foundation may be used to test whether sleep-related autonomic responses contribute unique prognostic value to conventional measures of cardiovascular risk.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

papers.title: Chronotypes in adult patients with bipolar disorder: unraveling the impact of ADHD comorbidity.
papers.abstract: This cross-sectional study investigates chronotypes in adult patients diagnosed with bipolar disorder (BD), both with and without comorbid attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Seventy euthymic BD patients were recruited, with 23 having comorbid ADHD. Clinical assessments included diagnostic interviews, mood scales, ADHD-specific scales, and the Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire. ADHD+ patients showed lower MEQ total scores, indicating a greater tendency towards eveningness. After Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction, HAM-A and MEQ total scores remained significantly different between the ADHD+ and ADHD - groups. In correlation analyses, age, duration of bipolar disorder, HAM-A, HAM-D, Wender-Utah, and ASRS scores remained associated with MEQ total score after FDR correction. Hospitalisation count and YMRS score did not. In the multivariable linear regression analysis, Wender-Utah total score, HAM-D score, and duration of bipolar disorder remained significant predictors of MEQ score after FDR correction. This study provides further evidence of differences in chronotype-related measures among adult patients with bipolar disorder with and without comorbid ADHD. These findings suggest that ADHD and depressive symptom burden may be relevant to circadian rhythm in patients with bipolar disorder and highlight the importance of considering circadian characteristics in this population.
papers.journal: International journal of psychiatry in clinical practice

papers.title: Automated Interictal Epileptiform Discharge Detector Scores in Serial EEG: Record-Level Concordance Did Not Extend to Within-Participant Change.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveAutomated deep learning-based interictal epileptiform discharge detectors have been validated for cross-sectional recognition, but longitudinal concordance is uncertain. We tested whether three distinct pretrained detectors agreed on direction and rank ordering of within-participant change in serial EEG.MethodsThis secondary analysis included 45 routine EEG recordings from 15 adults with drug-resistant focal epilepsy at baseline, week 1, and month 3 in the active arm of a parent tDCS trial; treatment efficacy was not evaluated. SpikeNet1, SpikeNet2, and Cyclops used pretrained weights and detector-specific pipelines on identically staged 25-min intervals. The record-level endpoint was the unthresholded mean window score. Concordance was characterized using record-level and change-score Spearman correlations, directional agreement, and a standardized detector × time repeated-measures ANOVA.ResultsDescriptive record-level correlations ranged from ρ = 0.341 to 0.696. Change-score correlations ranged from -0.011 to 0.379 (week 1) and from -0.089 to 0.536 (month 3). All six were smaller in absolute magnitude than their record-level counterparts and nonsignificant after Holm adjustment. Three-detector directional agreement was 7/15 (week 1) and 6/15 (month 3). The detector × time interaction was nonsignificant (Greenhouse-Geisser-corrected p = .142). Post hoc tolerance zones did not increase three-detector agreement. Thresholded SpikeNet2 and Cyclops outputs were sparse, and high-threshold agreement reflected shared zero change.ConclusionsRecord-level concordance did not extend to within-participant change or establish longitudinal interchangeability of mean window scores. Even for validated detectors, a longitudinal finding from one detector should not be assumed to generalize across detectors without independent corroboration.Parent trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05951244), NCT05951244.

papers.title: Predicting Seizure Recurrence After Withdrawal of Antiseizure Medications Through Electroencephalogram Connectivity Analysis: A Proof-of-Concept Study.
papers.abstract: BackgroundDetermining antiseizure medication (ASM) withdrawal in patients with prolonged seizure freedom is crucial, yet no reliable biomarker exists. Pediatric neurologists often rely on clinical risk factors and electroencephalogram (EEG) inspection to predict recurrence.MethodsWe applied EEG connectivity analysis using directed transfer function (DTF) to predict recurrence after ASM withdrawal in 63 patients (29 recurrence, 34 nonrecurrence). All patients were seizure-free for at least 2 years before their ASMs were withdrawn. Before ASM withdrawal, an EEG was obtained for each patient, and indicated the absence of epileptiform discharges. Classification was conducted with feature selection and five classifiers.ResultsThe statistical results revealed that the DTF connectivity in the motor regions, including the right primary motor cortex (Brodmann area 4, BA4) and the left and right medial premotor regions (Brodmann area 6, BA6), was significantly higher in the recurrence group. The highest average performance across the five evaluated classifiers (sensitivity, 87.50%; specificity, 87.35%; accuracy, 87.28%; and AUC, 87.43%) was achieved when 16 DTF features were selected. Compared with the majority-class baseline of 53.97% (representing the proportion of the majority non-recurrence class, 34/63), all trained classifiers demonstrated vastly superior performance. Among these classifiers, SVM had the best individual performance index, achieving a sensitivity of 96.67%, specificity of 90.58%, accuracy of 93.36%, and AUC of 93.63% while 16 selected features were used.ConclusionsThe method effectively identified Brodmann areas with significant differences and built models distinguishing recurrence from nonrecurrence at the patient level.

papers.title: Reconsidering attack frequency in hypnic headache: Implications for future ICHD diagnostic criteria.
papers.abstract: Hypnic headache (HH) is a rare primary headache disorder characterized by recurrent attacks that occur exclusively during sleep and awaken the patient. According to the current International Classification of Headache Disorders (ICHD), a diagnosis of definite HH requires attacks occurring on ≥10 days per month for >3 months. Although this threshold may improve diagnostic specificity, its empirical basis appears limited and derives largely from early case series and expert consensus rather than from systematic validation studies. Emerging clinical and epidemiological observations suggest that some patients with otherwise typical HH phenotypes experience attacks less frequently and therefore do not meet current criteria for definite HH. However, it remains unclear whether such cases represent the same disorder, a milder or early-stage phenotype, or a distinct clinical entity. In this Perspective, we review the evolution of HH diagnostic criteria, summarize available evidence regarding attack frequency and duration, and discuss methodological challenges inherent to diagnostic criteria development in disorders lacking objective biomarkers. We argue that the recurring lower-frequency phenotype among patients currently classified as having probable HH supports recognition of episodic HH. We propose retaining the current ICHD-3 definition unchanged as chronic HH and adding episodic HH for patients who fulfil all remaining criteria but experience attacks on 1-9 days per month for >3 months. In parallel, we propose alternative Appendix criteria requiring at least 10 lifetime attacks without a specified monthly-frequency requirement to facilitate prospective validation. This framework preserves the established HH phenotype while enabling systematic study of lower-frequency cases. Furthermore, it could give further insights into the clinical spectrum of HH and possibly shed some light on pathophysiological mechanisms.
papers.journal: Cephalalgia : an international journal of headache

papers.title: Foslevodopa/Foscarbidopa and Objective Physical Activity in a Patient With Advanced Parkinson's Disease and Pre-Existing Hallucinations.
papers.abstract: We describe a patient with advanced Parkinson's disease (PD) and pre-existing hallucinations who underwent continuous subcutaneous infusion (CSCI) of foslevodopa/foscarbidopa (LDP/CDP) and whose accelerometer metrics of physical activity improved following treatment. Four and six weeks after 24 h/day CSCI of LDP/CDP, the metabolic equivalent of task (MET), total moderate and vigorous physical activity (MVPA) and percentage of MVPA, and step counts increased. A decrease in the total time of sedentary bouts, total sedentary bouts, daily average of sedentary bouts, and maximum length of sedentary bouts and an increase in the movement index during the night were observed. The 24-h CSCI of LDP/CDP can be advantageous in that it objectively reduces periods of inactivity and increases physical activity, which may be due to the expectation that the CSCI of LDP/CDP may lessen the wearing-off phenomenon.

papers.title: An assessment of quality and reliability: sleep disorder information in short videos on major social platforms.
papers.abstract: Short video platforms have become a primary source of health information. This study aimed to assess the quality and reliability of sleep-disorder-related content on two major Chinese platforms, Douyin and Bilibili. In this cross-sectional study, the top-ranked videos meeting the inclusion and exclusion criteria were retrieved from each platform between September 27 and October 1, 2025 by entering the single Chinese-language query "" ("sleep disorder insomnia"; one space between the terms and no Boolean operator). After screening, 200 videos (100 per platform) were assessed by two psychiatrists, with a third evaluator adjudicating discrepancies. Quality and reliability were evaluated using the Global Quality Scale (GQS) and a modified DISCERN (mDISCERN) tool. Video content completeness, source (experts, non-experts, science communication accounts, and individual users), engagement metrics, and platform differences were analyzed using non-parametric tests, including Dunn's post hoc test with Bonferroni correction for pairwise group comparisons. Content-completeness assessment showed that symptoms received some content in 73% of videos and substantive content in 14.5%, whereas epidemiology and etiology received no content in 56.5% and 52.0%, respectively. Douyin videos had higher user engagement (likes and shares) and higher quality scores (median GQS: 3 vs. 2, p < 0.001) than Bilibili videos in this sample. GQS scores differed across publisher types, with individual-user videos scoring lowest in the significant pairwise comparisons; expert-authored videos had higher mDISCERN scores than non-expert and science-communication videos but did not differ significantly from individual-user videos. On both platforms, mDISCERN scores, but not GQS scores, showed positive exploratory associations with engagement metrics at the nominal p < 0.05 level. Sleep-disorder-related information in highly visible short videos was often incomplete, with greater coverage of symptoms than of epidemiology or etiology. In this convenience sample, Douyin videos had higher engagement and quality scores than Bilibili videos; however, publisher composition differed between platforms, and the cross-sectional design does not permit causal or platform-wide conclusions. Some pairwise comparisons favored expert-authored videos, but the pattern was not consistent across instruments and source groups. Higher mDISCERN scores were associated with engagement metrics on both platforms, although these exploratory associations do not establish their direction or underlying mechanisms.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "Sleep duration, sleep-wake schedules, and social jetlag among corporate employees in Japan: Age- and gender-based comparisons of wearable device data (2019-2022)" [Prevent. Med. Rep. 71 (2026) 103639].
papers.abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.1016/j.pmedr.2026.103639.].

papers.title: Stress and insomnia severity in relation to sleep quality among shift-working nursing staff: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Sleep is an integral component of normal functioning, enabling rest and physiological recovery. Due to the nature of shift work, nursing staff are particularly vulnerable to disruptions of circadian rhythms. Shift work may substantially contribute to poorer sleep quality, the development of insomnia, and increased perceived stress levels. Disruption of the biological sleep rhythm may result in impaired normal functioning. The consequences may include not only deterioration of health but also impaired awareness and concentration, thereby significantly affecting the level and quality of care provided to patients. Despite the growing body of research, there remains a lack of comprehensive analyses simultaneously assessing the broad spectrum of relationships between sleep, insomnia, and stress among nursing staff. The aim of the study was to assess the relationship between perceived stress levels and the severity of insomnia symptoms and sleep quality among nursing staff working in a shift system. The study was conducted using a diagnostic survey method and had a cross-sectional design. The respondents were nursing staff employed in the departments of the Fryderyk Chopin University Clinical Hospital in Rzeszów. An original questionnaire and standardized research instruments were used: the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10), the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). The statistical analysis included descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and multiple linear regression using the stepwise method. Among the study group of 247 nursing staff members working in a shift system, sleep disturbances and insomnia symptoms were common. Poor sleep quality was identified in 76.1% of respondents, while 81.4% of participants obtained an ISI score of ≥8 points, indicating the presence of insomnia symptoms of at least subthreshold severity. Higher perceived stress scores were associated with greater severity of insomnia symptoms and poorer sleep quality. The strongest association was observed between insomnia symptom severity and sleep quality. Multivariable analysis confirmed significant associations between insomnia symptom severity, perceived stress, and sleep quality. Sleep problems were common among the shift-working nursing staff included in the study. Perceived stress was significantly associated with insomnia symptom severity and poorer sleep quality. The findings support the importance of early identification of sleep problems and consideration of stress management in initiatives aimed at supporting the wellbeing of shift-working nursing staff.

papers.title: Circadian Clock: A Non-Negligible Role in Hypertension-Associated Ischemic Stroke.
papers.abstract: Hypertension and ischemic stroke (IS) are prevalent circulatory system disorders. Notably, hypertension is a major risk factor for IS, with approximately 70% of IS patients having a documented history of hypertension. Meanwhile, studies have demonstrated that antihypertensive therapy reduces IS recurrence risk by 19-22%; however, nearly half of patients still exhibit inadequate blood pressure (BP) control. The circadian clock, an endogenous timing system synchronized to the 24-hour light-dark cycle, exerts multiple protective effects on the cardiovascular and cerebrovascular systems through spatiotemporal regulatory mechanisms, including the regulation of diurnal BP rhythms, suppression of neuroinflammation, maintenance of blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, modulation of coagulation functions, and attenuation of vascular endothelial cell (EC) senescence. These insights provide novel perspectives for the prevention and treatment of hypertension-associated IS. This review elaborates on the composition and functional mechanisms of the circadian clock and discusses the role of circadian rhythm in hypertension and IS comorbidity, particularly how circadian dysregulation contributes to the elevated incidence and severity of IS in hypertensive individuals. Furthermore, this review critically evaluates circadian-based therapeutic strategies, including chronopharmacological approaches and lifestyle interventions, while acknowledging that most of these strategies remain in preclinical or early clinical investigation. These insights may provide novel perspectives for future research into the prevention and management of hypertension-associated IS.

papers.title: Intraoperative Subcallosal Cingulate Local Field Potential Spectral Analysis During Emotion-Evoking Music in Treatment-Resistant Depression With Multitarget Deep Brain Stimulation: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: The subcallosal cingulate (SCC/sgACC) is a proposed target for deep brain stimulation (DBS) in treatment-resistant depression (TRD), and intraoperative local field potentials (LFPs) are being explored as a source of candidate biomarkers. We report a 52-year-old woman with early-onset, highly refractory TRD and comorbid obsessive-compulsive and anxiety disorders who underwent tractography-guided multitarget DBS with four 8-contact non-directional leads: two in the SCC and two along a trajectory through the posterior-ventral nucleus accumbens (NAc), the anterior bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST), and the anterior limb of the internal capsule (ALIC). In this exploratory technical observation, LFPs were recorded from the macrocontact of a microelectrode in the left SCC of the awake patient, with stimulation OFF, during two music trials: one with a no-music baseline, two neutral songs (rock and classical), and her favorite (happy) song, and one with a baseline and a sad song. Spectra (Welch's method) and aperiodic exponents were compared post hoc, and broadband (3-45 Hz) power during each song was expressed relative to the baseline of the same trial. Verification of the raw data identified non-neural features that could mimic affective effects: the exported segments had been downsampled without anti-alias filtering, so 60-Hz mains interference appeared as narrow lines at 40 and 20 Hz, and 23 corrupted samples in the first 4 s of the happy-song segment inflated its power more than 200-fold. After their exclusion, broadband power relative to baseline was higher during the sad song (1.43-fold) than during the happy song (0.69-fold; between-song ratio 2.06, permutation p=0.024) and the rock song (0.57-fold; ratio 2.48, p=0.004), but not the classical piece (1.13-fold; p=0.45). Absolute power did not differ between the sad and happy songs, power rose transiently before the sad song began and remained elevated after it ended, and aperiodic exponents showed no valence-related pattern. Three months after stimulation onset, the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale score decreased from 26 to 13 and the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale score from 19 to 8. This single-case observation provides, at most, a weak post hoc signal of valence-related SCC broadband activity and mainly shows how acquisition and export artifacts can mimic affective LFP effects. Raw-data verification, anti-alias filtering, and repeated, counterbalanced conditions are prerequisites for evaluating intraoperative SCC LFPs as candidate biomarkers.

papers.title: Mind-body exercise and mental health in college students: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: College student populations show elevated psychological difficulties. Mind-body exercise, a non-pharmacological intervention, has attracted increasing attention, but direct comparisons of effectiveness across modalities remain limited. This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated the comparative efficacy of mindfulness-based exercise, Tai Chi, Baduanjin, yoga, and combined mind-body interventions on core mental health outcomes in college students. Following PRISMA-NMA guidelines, eligible RCTs were searched in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science. Risk of bias was assessed using the RoB 2 tool, and analyses were conducted in R with anxiety, depression, and stress as primary outcomes (SMD, 95% CrI). Twenty-four RCTs were included, covering five single interventions and one combined intervention (mindfulness-based exercise + Tai Chi). Network meta-analysis showed that for reducing anxiety, Baduanjin (SMD = -0.53, 95% CrI: -0.96 to -0.10), mindfulness-based exercise (SMD = -0.70, -0.98 to -0.44), Tai Chi (SMD = -0.61, -1.22 to -0.07), yoga (SMD = -0.47, -0.85 to -0.11), and the combined intervention (SMD = -0.99, -2.00 to -0.01) were significantly effective. For depression, Baduanjin (SMD = -0.75, -1.10 to -0.36) and mindfulness-based exercise (SMD = -0.55, -0.82 to -0.29) were superior. For stress, mindfulness-based exercise (SMD = -0.67, -0.91 to -0.47) and yoga (SMD = -0.32, -0.61 to -0.05) were effective, with mindfulness-based exercise outperforming yoga. No intervention significantly improved mental well-being or sleep quality compared with controls. However, this lack of statistically significant benefit does not rule out genuine intervention effects, and these findings remain inconclusive given the limited evidence. Mind-body exercises exert differential effects. Baduanjin may relieve anxiety and depression, while mindfulness-based exercise is beneficial for reducing stress.

papers.title: Reduced entorhinal and dentate theta-gamma coupling associated with adult Reelin loss in Alzheimer's disease relevant mice.
papers.abstract: Early Alzheimer's disease (AD) affects entorhinal-hippocampal circuits, motivating functional measures of altered network coordination. We examined local field potentials and multiunit activity in head-fixed mice in a virtual-reality (VR) environment, comparing WT, AppNL-F, and AppNL-F-Reln-cKO groups (n = 3 male mice per genotype). Reelin deletion was induced in adulthood using a ubiquitous tamoxifen-inducible Cre driver and was not restricted to entorhinal cortex (EC). Recordings sampled EC, dentate gyrus (DG), and CA1. Theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling was quantified using modulation index (MI) and phase-locking value (PLV) between theta phase and the phase of the gamma-amplitude envelope. Nominal genotype effects were detected for DG-theta/DG-gamma coupling (MI, p = 0.034; PLV, p = 0.035) and EC-theta/DG-gamma coupling (MI, p = 0.0043; PLV, p = 0.0079), with descriptively lower means in AppNL-F-Reln-cKO mice. Regional power spectra appeared broadly similar; a nominal genotype effect was reported for DG theta power (p = 0.029), rather than a selective DG gamma-power reduction. Exploratory analyses suggested stronger coupling attenuation in the 35-55-Hz range and lower DG-associated coupling in both high and low theta/delta states. These findings identify DG-associated theta-gamma coupling as a candidate functional readout of adult Reelin loss in an AD-relevant background. The small cohort, uncorrected comparisons, widespread deletion, and absence of coupling-behavior analyses limit anatomical and functional inference.

papers.title: ccPAS as a platform for biomarker-informed precision motor neurorehabilitation: a mini review.
papers.abstract: Inter-individual variability remains a major obstacle to translating non-invasive neuromodulation into rehabilitation. Cortico-cortical paired associative stimulation (ccPAS) is usually considered a tool for inducing pathway-specific plasticity, but its timing, direction and state dependence (and the possibility of measuring physiological responses during and after stimulation) may also make it useful for interrogating how an individual circuit responds. In this Mini Review, we examine ccPAS across applications to identify evidence relevant to biomarker-informed personalization, with a focus on premotor-motor pathways from the ventral premotor cortex (PMv) and supplementary/pre-supplementary motor area (SMA/preSMA) to primary motor cortex (M1). Our updated search identified 72 original reports applying repeated paired stimulation to two cortical (or cerebellar-cortical) sites, 25 of which targeted PMv → M1 or SMA/preSMA→M1 pathways. We synthesize evidence on spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP)-like effects, online physiological responses, transcranial magnetic stimulation-electroencephalography (TMS-EEG) and connectivity measures, structural pathway integrity, state dependence and dose. Rather than treating response variability only as a limitation, we ask whether measurable differences in pathway responsiveness could provide information for tailoring stimulation. Translational evidence remains predominantly mechanistic, although repeated SMA → M1 ccPAS has shown clinical and network-level effects after stroke. We propose a cautious framework in which baseline pathway assessment, a calibration stage, individualized stimulation parameters and post-intervention monitoring could support future precision motor neurorehabilitation.

papers.title: What shared responses reveal about audience behavior: neural prediction and the emerging potential of peripheral synchrony.
papers.abstract: Predicting audience responses to dynamic media remains a significant challenge in neuromarketing and neuroforecasting. Intersubject correlation (ISC) has been proposed to address this need by quantifying the temporal similarity of neural, physiological, and behavioral responses among individuals exposed to the same stimulus. This narrative mini-review examines how ISC relates to preferences, judgments, and behavior and proposes a conceptual framework for interpreting its predictive value. Across modalities, ISC consistently reflects shared stimulus processing and is associated with attention, alongside additional links to engagement, memory, and higher-order narrative processing. Neural ISC has shown associations with individual, group, and population-level outcomes, although findings vary by neural modality, analytic approach, and behavioral endpoint. Peripheral ISC derived from gaze, heart rate, electrodermal activity, and facial expressions provides complementary information about interindividual alignment, but direct evidence for predicting consumer outcomes remains limited. At the same time, neural and peripheral measures capture various aspects of shared response dynamics, and combining them in a multimodal ISC approach may help distinguish synchronization in different functional domains, including perceptual, attentional, autonomic, affective, and valuation-related processes, and clarify their relationship to the target outcome. The proposed framework therefore conceptualizes ISC as a probabilistic predictor whose predictive value depends on which functional processes underlie the observed synchrony and their relevance to the specific outcome of interest.

papers.title: Electrocardiographic P-Wave Parameters as Predictors of Non-Dipper Blood Pressure Pattern in Hypertensive Patients.
papers.abstract: Non-dipper blood pressure (BP) patterns are linked to an increased risk of cardiovascular issues, however the specific relationship between these patterns and electrocardiographic (ECG) findings remains unclear. This study aimed to explore the predictive value of P wave parameters in identifying non-dipper BP patterns among hypertensive patients. We conducted a retrospective study involving 497 hypertensive individuals who underwent 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring (ABPM) and standard 12-lead ECG. Participants were classified as dipper or non-dipper based on changes in nighttime BP. We evaluated various ECG parameters including P wave duration, amplitude, dispersion, and peak time in leads V1 (PWPTV1) and II (PWPTD2). Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis were used to determine independent predictors of non-dipper status. Of the total participants, 332 exhibited a non-dipper pattern. In multivariable analysis, a history of hypertension, prolonged PWPTV1 and prolonged PWPTD2 were found to independently predict non-dipper status (all p < 0.01). ROC curve analysis demonstrated moderate predictive ability with an area under the curve of 0.68 for PWPTV1 and 0.64 for PWPTD2. The findings indicate that PWPTV1 and PWPTD2 are straightforward non-invasive ECG measurements that may serve as indicators of a non-dipper BP pattern in hypertensive patients. This suggests a potential role for ECG in clinical assessments in situations where ABPM is not available.

papers.title: Dynamic stiffening of brain states: a neurodynamic framework of functional adaptation, impaired transitions, and neuromodulation.
papers.abstract: Contemporary approaches in systems neuroscience describe the brain as a nonlinear dynamical system capable of adopting multiple transient functional configurations. Within this perspective, functional impairment may concern not only the properties of individual brain states but also the capacity to transition between them when contextual demands change. We propose a theoretical framework centred on dynamic stiffening, defined as impaired context-dependent accessibility of transitions between functional brain configurations. This phenomenon is not restricted to oscillatory activity or to a single neurobiological mechanism. The progressive stabilisation of an initially adaptive response represents one possible pathway, alongside alterations in connectivity, plasticity, or regulatory processes. Thalamocortical interactions constitute one plausible substrate, while EEG provides an accessible, though indirect, means of investigating neural reconfiguration. The central experimentally testable prediction is that, when cognitive or environmental demands require neural reconfiguration, individuals exhibiting the hypothesised dynamic-stiffening phenotype will show reduced probabilities or increased latencies of transitions towards functionally appropriate neural configurations compared with suitable controls, even when the overall repertoire of observed configurations remains relatively preserved. Alterations in state diversity, persistence, and recovery dynamics are considered complementary rather than necessary features. The framework outlines experimentally testable predictions and conditions for falsification, distinguishing adaptive stability, impaired transition accessibility, and excessive instability. Finally, it proposes that neurofeedback and neuromodulation could be investigated as potential means of modifying transition dynamics, while recognising that their causal and therapeutic relevance remains to be established.

papers.title: Sleep quality, social jet lag, and cardiovascular risk factors in young adults.
papers.abstract: Sleep quality, along with dietary and behavioral patterns, influences cardiovascular health, and its insufficiency can increase cardiometabolic risk. This study aimed to analyze the association between sleep quality and cardiovascular risk factors in university students, considering anthropometric, clinical, and biochemical indicators as well as dietary patterns. This cross-sectional observational study included 243 undergraduate Nutrition students from public and private institutions in Fortaleza, Ceará, Brazil, participating in the Nutritionist Health Study. Sociodemographic, lifestyle, anthropometric, blood pressure, and laboratory data were collected. Sleep quality was assessed with the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and chronotype and social jet lag (SJL) with the Munich Chronotype Questionnaire (MCTQ). Food consumption was estimated with a validated Food Frequency Questionnaire and classified according to the NOVA system. Statistical analyses included Pearson and Spearman correlations and multiple linear regression adjusted for sociodemographic and lifestyle variables, with p < 0.05 considered significant. The mean overall PSQI score was 6.5 ± 3.0 and 144 participants (59.3%) had PSQI >5, indicating poor sleep quality. Mean sleep duration was 7 h 12 min, mean chronotype was 4 h 13 min, and SJL was 1 h 25 min. Ultra-processed food consumption was positively associated with a later chronotype (β = 0.209; p = 0.001; q = 0.016). Waist circumference was positively correlated with poorer sleep quality and shorter sleep duration; and body mass index was positively associated with shorter sleep duration. University students presented predominantly poor sleep quality and a later chronotype associated with higher consumption of ultra-processed foods and unfavorable metabolic markers. These findings suggest an association between dietary patterns, circadian rhythm, and cardiovascular risk, highlighting the importance of integrated strategies that promote adequate sleep and a balanced diet as early initiatives for cardiometabolic prevention.

papers.title: Visceral Adipose Tissue and Cardiac Arrhythmogenesis: Current Mechanistic Evidence and Clinical Implications.
papers.abstract: Visceral adiposity is increasingly recognized as a biologically relevant determinant of arrhythmic risk that is only partially captured by body mass index. The pathophysiological signal arises from both systemic adipose dysfunction and regional ectopic fat deposition, particularly epicardial adipose tissue, which lies in direct continuity with the atrial and ventricular myocardium. In contemporary literature, the association between adiposity and atrial fibrillation is no longer explained solely by chamber enlargement, hypertension, diabetes, or sleep apnea. Instead, obesity-related arrhythmogenesis appears to reflect, at least in part, an integrated atrial myopathy characterized by inflammatory activation, oxidative stress, fibrofatty remodeling, conduction heterogeneity, autonomic imbalance, and altered electromechanical coupling. Regional visceral and pericardial fat predict incident atrial fibrillation beyond general adiposity, while histological, imaging, and electroanatomical studies support a plausible contribution of epicardial adipose tissue to atrial fibrosis, low-voltage substrate, and post-ablation recurrence. Contemporary imaging studies also suggest that depot location and qualitative characteristics, such as tissue attenuation or density, may be as important as absolute fat volume. Therapeutically, durable weight loss and structured risk factor modification are associated with reverse remodeling of components of the arrhythmogenic substrate. In contrast, pharmacological strategies that reduce or modulate epicardial adipose tissue remain promising but require further prospective validation. Data for ventricular arrhythmias are emerging but remain substantially less mature, largely confined to observational studies and mechanistic inference. This review synthesizes current evidence on the relationship between visceral adiposity, epicardial fat, and cardiac arrhythmias.

papers.title: Cardiovascular Abnormalities in Daily Life: Digital Monitoring, Wearables, and the Early Course of Disease.
papers.abstract: Wearable devices and other forms of digital monitoring have extended cardiovascular observation beyond the clinic; however, the clinical value of these devices is not captured by describing them merely as convenient versions of Holter monitors, blood pressure cuffs, or pulse oximeters. Their distinctive contribution lies in repeated measurement during ordinary life, across sleep, activity, recovery, symptoms, and day-to-day physiological variation. This shifts the clinical question. Instead of asking only whether a cardiovascular abnormality is present at the time of testing, clinicians may begin to ask how an abnormality develops, fluctuates, and resolves within the baseline and lived context of an individual. Atrial fibrillation provides the clearest proof of concept, because wearable-based detection is clinically meaningful only when photoplethysmography-derived alerts are recognized as screening signals, followed by electrocardiographic confirmation, and integrated into risk-based clinical care. Large, pragmatic studies and contemporary guidance now support several components of this pathway. Yet the significance of digital cardiovascular medicine extends beyond atrial fibrillation. Heart failure decompensation, blood pressure lability and autonomic fluctuation, sleep-related cardiovascular burden, and the evaluation of palpitations or nonspecific symptoms may all benefit from longitudinal, context-rich observation. False positives, uncertain actionability, user anxiety, data overload, uneven access, and weak interoperability remain substantial constraints. The mature clinical promise of the field lies not in technology alone, but in enabling cardiovascular abnormalities to be examined in daily life, during their early course, and in relation to the individual in whom they occur.

papers.title: Factors associated with cognitive frailty among community-dwelling older adults with olfactory impairment: a cross-sectional study in China.
papers.abstract: To explore the influencing factors of cognitive frailty among community-dwelling older adults with olfactory impairment. Convenience sampling was adopted to recruit 419 older adults with olfactory impairment from three communities in Changchun City between March 2025 and March 2026. Data were collected using a general information questionnaire, Fried Frailty Phenotype Scale, Chinese version of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment, Family APGAR Index, Short Form Mini Nutritional Assessment, SARC-CalF, Short Geriatric Depression Scale, Oral Frailty Index-8, and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Multivariable Logistic regression analysis was applied to identify the influencing factors of cognitive frailty in community-dwelling older adults with olfactory impairment. Among 419 older adults with olfactory impairment, 102 had both physical frailty and mild cognitive impairment and were classified as having cognitive frailty (24.34%), while 116 had physical frailty alone, 61 had mild cognitive impairment alone, and 140 had neither condition. Significant between-group differences were found in age, hand grip strength, sex, marital status, sarcopenia screening result, nutritional status, oral frailty, and sleep quality (p < 0.05). In the primary multivariable logistic regression model, higher hand grip strength was associated with lower odds of cognitive frailty, whereas unmarried status, risk of sarcopenia, risk of malnutrition, and high risk of oral frailty were associated with higher odds of cognitive frailty (p < 0.05). Sensitivity analyses showed generally consistent associations for the other explanatory variables; however, hand grip strength was no longer significantly associated with CF after additional adjustment for age and sex. No evidence of multicollinearity was observed among variables retained in the primary model (VIF range: 1.078-1.132). The primary model demonstrated an AUC of 0.75 (95% CI: 0.69-0.80), with an optimal cut-off value of 0.195, sensitivity of 0.755, and specificity of 0.615. The prevalence of cognitive frailty was relatively high among community-dwelling older adults with olfactory impairment, and several factors were associated with cognitive frailty. Therefore, community administrators should prioritize the screening and assessment of cognitive frailty among older adults with OI, particularly those with factors associated with higher odds of cognitive frailty. These findings may help identify high-risk individuals and inform the development of targeted health management strategies.

papers.title: Conduction System Pacing in Children: Current Evidence and Considerations for Lifelong Physiological Pacing.
papers.abstract: Conduction system pacing (CSP) is a potential physiological alternative to conventional right ventricular pacing for children expected to require long-term ventricular stimulation. CSP is most relevant in congenital or postoperative atrioventricular block and congenital heart disease (CHD), where lifelong pacing, repeat procedures, venous preservation, and pacing-related ventricular dysfunction are major concerns. This narrative review synthesises the available paediatric and congenital CSP literature, with a separate appraisal of His bundle pacing (HBP), left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP), conventional right ventricular pacing, epicardial pacing, and cardiac resynchronisation therapy (CRT). Evidence remains limited to small observational cohorts, mixed paediatric and adult congenital series, and case reports. The available data indicate procedural feasibility in selected children of school age, adolescents, and CHD populations. LBBAP has generally shown lower chronic capture thresholds than HBP in mixed paediatric cohorts, while data supporting recovery of ventricular function after CSP are uncontrolled and limited to selected patients. No paediatric randomised trial has established CSP as superior to optimised epicardial pacing, conventional transvenous pacing, or CRT for long-term clinical outcomes. Children differ from adults in septal thickness, cardiac anatomy, growth, venous access, future lead burden, and extraction planning. Therefore, CSP should be considered an individualised strategy within experienced paediatric and congenital electrophysiology programmes, with explicit documentation of capture, lead position, and long-term device planning.

papers.title: Case Report: Clinical applications of extended-duration remote ambulatory EEG monitoring: lessons from real-world cases.
papers.abstract: Traditional ambulatory electroencephalography (EEG) and inpatient epilepsy monitoring unit (EMU) admissions face significant operational limitations including: short recording windows (typically 24-72 h), high costs, technician shortages, and physical restrictions on daily activities. This article presents clinical utility frameworks and three illustrative real-world case studies utilizing the REMI Remote EEG Monitoring System-a wireless, wearable 4-sensor electrode-setup (10-channel EEG montage system) montage system integrated with cloud data transmission and post-acquisition artificial intelligence (AI) electrographic seizure detection algorithms. In Case 1, a 39-year-old female with suspected recurrent epilepsy experienced three focal seizures after the standard 72-h monitoring window, allowing initiation of targeted antiseizure therapy. In Case 2, extended monitoring in a 57-year-old male with long-standing epilepsy experiencing new exercise-induced symptoms ruled out electrographic seizures, avoiding unnecessary medication escalation. In Case 3, a 52-year-old male with worsening episodic déjà vu exhibited focal interictal rhythmic activity, providing objective data to guide shared decision-making and successful initiation of antiseizure treatment. Extended-duration remote EEG monitoring bridges key diagnostic gaps by offering flexible, real-world data collection over extended timeframes (up to 30 days). This approach optimizes clinical triage, clarifies event etiology, and improves ambulatory epilepsy care without overburdening tertiary health care infrastructure.

papers.title: Thin illusion: a cross-sectional study on normal weight obesity among adults in a subdivision of Northern Haryana.
papers.abstract: While body mass index (BMI) is widely used to assess obesity, it fails to detect individuals with normal weight who have excess body fat referred to as normal weight obesity (NWO). NWO is associated with an increased risk of cardiometabolic conditions despite a seemingly healthy BMI. South Asians, known to carry higher fat percentages at lower BMI levels, are particularly susceptible. Yet, population-based data on the prevalence and determinants of NWO in North India are limited. To estimate the prevalence and examine the determinants of NWO among adults in Kurukshetra, North India, using Asian BMI criteria and body fat percentage. A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted from October 2022 to September 2023, involving 460 adults aged 20-60 years from urban (Shahabad) and rural (Thol) areas of Kurukshetra district, selected via multistage stratified random sampling. NWO was defined as BMI 18.50-22.99 kg/m² with body fat >25% in males and >30% in females, measured using an Omron body fat analyser. Data on sociodemographic, dietary, physical activity and sleep variables were collected using a pre-tested structured questionnaire. Associations were analysed using χ2 tests and multivariate logistic regression. NWO was identified in 24.6% of participants with normal BMI. The condition was more prevalent among females (27.6%) and increased notably with age, particularly after 40 years. Married individuals were more frequently affected. Protective factors included daily intake of fruits and vegetables, greater dietary diversity and moderate-to-high physical activity. Poor sleep hygiene, particularly prolonged sleep latency and short sleep duration, was also significantly associated with NWO. These findings suggest a hidden metabolic risk among individuals with otherwise 'normal' weight. NWO poses a significant but under-recognised public health challenge. Routine screening should include body fat assessments alongside BMI to enable early lifestyle interventions and prevent non-communicable diseases.

papers.title: Sleep position, respiratory event rates, and nocturnal oxygenation in a clinical monitoring cohort: a positional phenotyping analysis.
papers.abstract: Sleep position may affect respiratory events and nocturnal oxygenation, but positional event rates and their contributions relative to monitoring duration remain incompletely characterised. We retrospectively analysed 320 Level III portable respiratory monitoring records from a single-centre clinical cohort. Overall REI was ≥5 events/h in 249 participants. Supine and non-supine rates were compared in 317 participants with recordings in both positions. POSA classification was assessed in 219 participants with REI ≥5 events/h and at least 30 min of monitoring in each position; central apnoeas were excluded. POSA was defined by a supine event rate at least twice the non-supine rate. Supine versus non-supine median respiratory event rates were 22.73 versus 5.05 events/h, and desaturation rates were 7.12 versus 1.86 events/h (both p < 0.001). POSA was identified in 142/219 participants (64.8%). Compared with non-POSA participants, those with POSA had higher minimum SpO₂ (83.5% versus 78.0%, p = 0.004), fewer desaturation events (48.5 versus 85.0, p = 0.035), and lower REI (27.35 versus 42.14 events/h, p = 0.001). REI correlated with minimum SpO₂ (ρ = -0.465) and cumulative desaturation duration (ρ = 0.644). Among 304 participants, supine positioning represented 57.0% of monitoring duration but 73.7% of respiratory and 74.3% of desaturation events. Supine positioning was associated with higher event rates and a disproportionate event contribution in this clinical monitoring cohort. POSA findings apply only to eligible participants. Position-specific measures may complement conventional indices but do not establish treatment effects.

papers.title: Temporal misalignment in rheumatoid arthritis: a model linking microbial metabolic rhythms, circadian clocks, and inflammatory timing.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) exhibits pronounced time-of-day variation in inflammatory activity, including nocturnal cytokine elevation and early-morning symptom exacerbation. Although circadian disruption, gut microbial alterations, and immune dysregulation have each been implicated in RA, these processes have largely been studied as temporally independent phenomena. Here, we propose the temporal misalignment model, which reframes RA inflammatory timing as a disturbance in the relative timing among gut microbial metabolic rhythms, host circadian clocks, and immune effector processes. The model distinguishes three measurable dimensions of temporal organisation: inter-system phase relationships, oscillatory amplitude relevant to temporal coupling, and cross-system coherence. Microbiota-associated metabolites, including short-chain fatty acids, tryptophan-related metabolites, and bile acids are proposed as candidate mediators because they exhibit time-of-day variation and can modulate host clock-related pathways, although direct evidence for such coupling in human RA remains limited. The model predicts that cross-system temporal abnormalities may precede clinically apparent RA, contribute to heterogeneity in chronotherapy response, and propagate downstream when microbial rhythmicity is experimentally perturbed. Crucially, restoration of microbial rhythmicity without corresponding realignment of host clock, immune, and inflammatory timing would challenge the proposed causal framework. By treating temporal relationships as measurable biological variables, the temporal misalignment model extends existing neuroendocrine and gut-joint frameworks and provides a falsifiable basis for time-resolved mechanistic studies in RA.

papers.title: Development and pilot temporal validation of a questionnaire-free model for severe obstructive sleep apnea using sex, waist circumference, and TyG index.
papers.abstract: Current Knowledge/Study Rationale: Polysomnography (PSG) resources remain severely limited in primary care settings across China. Existing Western-derived questionnaire-based screening tools, such as the STOP-Bang questionnaire, are constrained by linguistic and cultural barriers when applied to Chinese populations, creating an urgent need for an objective, low-cost tool to identify patients with severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). We developed and validated a simple, questionnaire-free prediction model using three routine health-checkup parameters-sex, waist circumference, and the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index. In a temporal validation cohort, the model achieved a high sensitivity of 87.2% at a low cutoff, supporting its utility as a triage tool in Chinese primary care and health examination centers to reduce missed diagnoses of severe OSA.
