papers.title: Neurocognitive deficits in controlling aversive memory in insomnia disorder.
papers.abstract: Insomnia disorder is a common sleep disturbance characterized by cognitive hyperarousal, such as intrusive and uncontrollable thoughts (e.g. thoughts about sleeplessness, worries). Memory control, a key self-regulatory ability to control or inhibit unwanted thoughts and memories, plays an essential role in supporting cognitive functions and emotional well-being. Here, we delineate the neurocognitive mechanisms underlying memory control among individuals with insomnia. Forty-one participants meeting DSM-5 criteria for insomnia disorder and 40 healthy sleepers completed an emotional Think/No-Think task, during which they were instructed to either retrieve (Think), suppress the retrieval (No-Think) of aversive memories, or visually process cues without retrieval or suppress retrieval (Perceptual Baseline). At the same time, electroencephalographic (EEG) activity was recorded. Linear mixed model analyses with age and depression scores as covariates showed that the insomnia group exhibited impaired memory control abilities, as evidenced by reduced suppression-induced forgetting during memory recall compared with the healthy group. Electrophysiologically, the insomnia group showed enhanced P300, a well-established neural marker of conscious episodic retrieval, in the No-Think condition compared to the Perceptual Baseline condition, indicating residual episodic retrieval during memory suppression. In contrast, this difference was absent among the healthy group, suggesting successful inhibition or abolishment of the memory traces. Individuals with insomnia showed impaired memory control of aversive memories and aberrant electrophysiological activities during retrieval suppression. Future research shall investigate the neural mechanisms underlying memory control deficits in insomnia disorder and the causal relationship between memory control abilities and insomnia symptoms.

papers.title: Allosteric modulation of GluN2B-containing glutamate receptors reduces seizures in autoimmune encephalitis.
papers.abstract: Anti-N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (anti-NMDAR) encephalitis manifests with encephalopathy, seizures, cognitive impairment, and sleep disruption that respond poorly to conventional therapies; novel effective treatments are urgently needed. GluN2B-containing NMDARs play important roles in seizure generation and cognition; however, their contribution to anti-NMDAR encephalitis remains unclear. We investigated whether patient-derived anti-NMDAR antibodies alter synaptic GluN1 and GluN2B receptor expression and whether selective GluN2B inhibition affects seizures, memory, and sleep in a mouse model of anti-NMDAR encephalitis. Male C57BL/6 mice (8-12 weeks old, n = 9-11 per group) were continuously infused for 14 days with monoclonal anti-NMDAR antibodies derived from a patient with anti-NMDAR encephalitis or with control IgG. Seizures and sleep were monitored using continuous electroencephalographic recordings. Traxoprodil (10 mg/kg i.p., daily), a selective negative allosteric modulator of GluN2B, was administered throughout the infusion period. Locomotor activity, anxiety-like behavior, and memory were assessed using open field and object location paradigms. Synaptosomes were isolated from whole brain tissue and were processed for GluN1 and GluN2B protein expression by Western blot. Consistent with prior studies, 89% of anti-NMDAR antibody-exposed mice developed seizures, with a median of 8 seizures over 2 weeks (interquartile range = 3-18). Antibody-infused mice also demonstrated hippocampus-dependent memory impairment and reduced rapid eye movement (REM) sleep compared to control mice. Traxoprodil diminished seizures (p = .02) but did not alter memory and sleep dysfunction. Anti-NMDAR IgG exposure markedly reduced synaptic GluN1 and GluN2B protein expression, and traxoprodil prevented this (p = .0002 and p = .02, respectively). Our study demonstrates sleep disruption in an animal model of anti-NMDAR encephalitis and highlights the selective role of GluN2B signaling in seizure expression. The persistence of cognitive and sleep disruption during traxoprodil treatment suggests distinct pathophysiological mechanisms. Selective modulation of GluN2B may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for seizure management in anti-NMDAR encephalitis.

papers.title: Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation for Promoting Recovery of Consciousness in Patients With Early Disorders of Consciousness: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the potential short-term therapeutic effect of transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) on the recovery of consciousness in patients with early disorders of consciousness (DOC). A total of 60 patients with early DOC were randomly assigned, and 57 completed the primary outcome assessment and were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. The intervention group received 10 Hz tACS targeting the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), whereas the control group received sham stimulation. Participants in both groups continued to receive conventional rehabilitation therapy. Neurobehavioral and electrophysiological assessments were conducted at baseline and after 14 days of intervention using the Coma Recovery Scale-Revised (CRS-R), the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), electroencephalography (EEG), and mismatch negativity (MMN). For the primary outcome, the CRS-R score was significantly higher in the intervention group than in the control group (F = 4.187, p = 0.046, partial η2 = 0.072). Sensitivity analysis yielded findings consistent with the primary analysis (Z = -2.042, p = 0.041). Improvement in GCS score was also significantly greater in the intervention group compared with the control group (Z = -2.637, p = 0.008). Neuroelectrophysiological findings indicated a significantly greater improvement in MMN elicitation in the intervention group relative to the control group (Z = -2.111, p = 0.035). Although EEG grading demonstrated a trend toward improvement, no statistically significant difference between the groups was identified (Z = -1.329, p = 0.184). When combined with conventional rehabilitation, a 2-week course of 10 Hz tACS applied to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex was associated with short-term, baseline-adjusted improvements in recovery of consciousness and behavioral responses in patients with early DOC. These preliminary findings suggest that 10 Hz tACS targeting the DLPFC may represent a potential adjunctive strategy for facilitating consciousness recovery in early DOC. ISRCTN registration number: ISRCTN15236545.

papers.title: The utility of additional electrodes during stereo-electroencephalography for pediatric epilepsy surgery.
papers.abstract: There is increasing use of stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) for invasive seizure onset zone (SOZ) localization in children due to its broad, three-dimensional, network-based sampling and improved tolerability compared with other strategies of invasive electrodes. However, initial SEEG does not always result in definitive SOZ localization, and diagnostic yield varies depending on patient selection and institution-specific factors. This study explores the benefits of additional electrodes to define the SOZ during the same hospitalization when initial SEEG sampling is insufficient for surgical planning in children. A cohort of patients who underwent additional electrode placement during the same hospitalization was identified from a database of pediatric epilepsy surgery cases performed between 2015 and 2025. Charts were retrospectively reviewed to obtain variables of interest, including demographics, electrode placement, and surgical outcomes. Fourteen patients underwent additional electrode placement during the same hospitalization. Reasons for additional electrodes include refining surgical resection margins (50%), inconclusive lobar localization (42%), and inconclusive lateralization (7%). Patients had an average of 11 initial and 3 additional electrode arrays implanted. Patients were monitored for seizure activity on average for 7 days for initial electrodes and an additional 4 days following additional electrode implantation. Following SEEG evaluation, patients underwent either laser ablation (50%), surgical resection (42%), or both (8%). Two patients did not proceed to surgery. Of the 12 patients who underwent surgery, 9 patients (75%) had a most recent follow-up outcome of ILAE 1-3. Additional electrode placement during the same hospitalization in this pediatric SEEG cohort was well tolerated with few observed minor complications and is particularly useful when electrodes are added to define surgical margins. Insights from additional electrodes influence subsequent surgical strategy, allowing more limited resections or laser ablations. These findings may contribute to attaining best practices for additional electrode use in pediatric SEEG patients. Stereotactic electrode placement is being increasingly used to define seizure origin in children with medication-resistant epilepsy, but it can fail to localize seizures in some cases. Placement of additional electrodes during the same hospitalization was associated with few observed minor complications in children and can help refine the surgical plan, allowing for more targeted surgery and may prevent the need for a second epilepsy surgery.

papers.title: Ecological Patterns and Associations of Dietary and Lifestyle Behaviours Among Adolescents Across 45 Low- and Middle-Income Countries.
papers.abstract: Adolescence is a critical period for the establishment of health-related behaviours that are shaped by shared individual, social and contextual determinants. This study investigated the prevalence, regional distribution and ecological associations of dietary, physical activity, sedentary and sleep-related indicators among adolescents across 45 low- and middle-income countries. This ecological, cross-country study used secondary data from the Global School-based Student Health Survey (GSHS; 2015-2021) and the Brazilian National School Health Survey (PeNSE 2015). Country-level prevalence estimates were derived from individual survey responses, using the country as the unit of analysis. Indicators included daily fruit, vegetables and soft drink consumption; fast-food consumption of at least 1 day in the past week; frequent worry-related sleep disturbance; physical activity of at least 60 min on all 7 days; active travel; participation in physical education classes; and excessive sedentary behaviour. Regional comparisons and exploratory country-level linear regression models adjusted for macroeconomic indicators were performed. Regional differences were observed for fast-food consumption, worry-related sleep disturbance, active travel and excessive sedentary behaviour. The Eastern Mediterranean showed higher fast-food consumption and sedentary behaviour and lower active travel than several other WHO regions. At the country level, higher prevalence of daily vegetable consumption was associated with lower prevalence of worry-related sleep disturbance (adjusted β = -1.89) and higher prevalence of the physical activity indicator (adjusted β = 1.34). Adolescent health indicators varied substantially across WHO regions and demonstrated consistent ecological associations at the country level. While these findings should be interpreted within an exploratory, population-level framework, they highlight the importance of considering regional and socioeconomic contexts when evaluating population patterns of health behaviours to inform context-sensitive public health strategies.
papers.journal: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association

papers.title: Self-rated cognitive failures in young adults are associated with depression and sleep disturbances, not objective cognitive performance.
papers.abstract: Although older age is dominantly associated with cognitive complaints or mistakes, such failures are also prevalent but much less studied in the young population. Importantly, they might impact academic or occupational performance, sleep, or general affect and well-being. Therefore, the aim of the present study was to identify variables potentially contributing to cognitive failures in healthy young adults, including objective cognitive performance, sleep, and affective factors. 125 young adults (mean age: 21 years, SD = 2.29) completed a series of self-report questionnaires and performed neurocognitive tasks targeting memory and executive functions. Variables associated with cognitive failures were identified by correlation analysis and hierarchical multiple linear regression. We demonstrated that although the amount of self-reported cognitive failures was not associated with objective cognitive performance, it was significantly related to subjective sleep quality and depression. Our results indicate the importance of examining affective and sleep-related factors in the case of subjective cognitive complaints, as cognitive failures reflect worries about one's cognitive ability rather than actual cognitive functioning, even at a younger age. Not applicable.

papers.title: Sex-dependent associations of retinoic acid-related orphan receptor alpha (RORA) variants with autism spectrum disorder susceptibility and severity in Egyptian children.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition with a strong genetic basis and marked sex bias. The retinoic acid-related orphan receptor alpha (RORA) gene has been implicated in ASD through its roles in neurodevelopment, circadian regulation, and steroid hormone signaling; however, evidence from Middle Eastern and North African populations remains limited. This case-control study investigated the association of two RORA polymorphisms (rs11632098 and rs4774388) with ASD susceptibility and symptom severity in 480 Egyptian children with ASD and 426 controls. Genotype and allele distributions were evaluated under multiple inheritance models with adjustment for sex and age. Sex-stratified, haplotype, and linkage disequilibrium analyses were performed. Associations with ASD severity were examined using multivariable linear regression and analysis of covariance based on continuous Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS) scores. RORA rs4774388 showed the strongest association with ASD susceptibility, demonstrating significant associations across multiple inheritance models (P < 0.0001 for all), whereas rs11632098 showed significant associations under selected genetic models. Sex-stratified analyses revealed that rs11632098 was associated with ASD susceptibility only in males, whereas rs4774388 was associated with ASD susceptibility in both sexes. Multivariable analysis demonstrated that rs11632098, but not rs4774388, was independently associated with ASD symptom severity after adjustment for age, sex, and the alternate RORA variant, with TC heterozygotes exhibiting the highest adjusted CARS scores. Haplotype analyses identified significant associations with ASD susceptibility and severity despite modest linkage disequilibrium between the two variants. These findings suggest that RORA rs4774388 was primarily associated with ASD susceptibility, whereas rs11632098 was associated with both ASD susceptibility and variation in symptom severity in this cohort. These associations provide population-specific evidence regarding RORA genetic variation in ASD among Egyptian children, although the functional consequences of the investigated variants remain uncertain.

papers.title: The dietary inflammatory index and its associations with sleep, mental health, quality of life and aggressive behavior in Iranian female adolescents.
papers.abstract: The relationship between the inflammatory potential of foods and sleep, mental health, quality of life and aggressive behaviors is not well understood in Iranian female adolescents. We aimed to address this since there is a high prevalence of these factors in this population. In this cross-sectional study, Dietary data was collected from 670 participants using a food frequency questionnaire. Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) scores for all participants were calculated and the data was split into quartiles based upon this. Logistic regression was used to obtain odds ratios for quality of life, depression, aggression, insomnia, sleepiness across quartiles of DII and adjustments were applied for a range of confounders. Mean score of depression was significantly different between quartiles of DII score (P = 0.02), but this disappeared after adjusting for confounders. Insomnia scores had significant differences across quartiles of DII score only in adjusted models (P < 0.001). A significant difference was observed for daytime sleepiness score throughout quartiles of DII score in our model adjusted for age and energy (P = 0.04). A positive association was seen between DII score and odds of depression, even after adjusting for age and energy (OR = 1.96; 95% CI = 1.18-3.27, P = 0.02). We did not find significant associations between quartiles of DII and odds of poor quality of life, aggression, insomnia, and daytime sleepiness. In summary, our finding reveal higher DII scores are associated with depression and sleep disruption in female adolescents in Iran. Therefore, anti-inflammatory foods should be recommended for consumption in this population.

papers.title: Prevalence and inter-relationship of depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms and poor sleep quality and their associations with quality of life in patients with coronary heart disease: findings from a large nationwide survey.
papers.abstract: Patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) commonly experience depressive and anxiety symptoms, poor sleep quality, and low health-related quality of life (HRQoL). However, inter-relationships between such mental health problems at a symptom level and their associations with HRQoL among patients with CHD remain unclear. This study compared the prevalence and network structure of psychiatric symptoms between participants with and without CHD and examined the associations between these symptoms and HRQoL. We conducted a cross-sectional nationwide survey and applied propensity score matching (PSM) to balance demographic characteristics between the CHD and non-CHD groups. The study used standardized instruments for depressive and anxiety symptoms, sleep quality, and HRQoL, and employed network analysis to identify central and bridge symptoms. The analyses included a total of 1,027 patients with CHD and 2,048 matched controls. The CHD group showed significantly higher prevalence of depressive symptoms (71.9%, 95% CI: 69.0%-74.6%), anxiety symptoms (60.9%, 95% CI: 57.8%-63.9%), and poor sleep quality (43.8%, 95% CI: 40.8%-46.9%) compared to the non-CHD group (depressive symptoms: 52.1%, 95% CI: 49.9%-54.2%; anxiety symptoms: 42.2%, 95% CI: 40.1%-44.4%; poor sleep quality: 29.6%, 95% CI: 27.7%-31.7%; all p < 0.001). HRQoL was significantly lower in the CHD group (p < 0.001) than the non-CHD group. Network analysis revealed that "Feeling afraid" (GAD7) had the highest expected influence in both groups. In the CHD group, "Sleep efficiency" (PSQI3) also showed high expected influence, while "Suicidal ideation" (PHQ9) and "Feeling afraid" (GAD7) were identified as key bridge symptoms. In the non-CHD group, "Restlessness" (GAD5) and "Sad mood" (PHQ2) were the key bridge symptoms. In both groups, "Night awakenings" (PSQI2) and "Sleep quality" (PSQI1) were strongly linked to reduced HRQoL. Network comparison tests showed no significant group differences in either the depressive-anxiety-sleep symptom networks or the HRQoL-symptom networks. Participants with CHD showed more severe depressive and anxiety symptoms, poorer sleep quality, and lower HRQoL than those without CHD. No significant group differences were observed in either the symptom networks or the HRQoL-symptom networks, indicating broadly comparable symptom-level patterns across CHD status. These findings may inform psychological and sleep-related assessment and symptom monitoring in CHD populations, but longitudinal and interventional studies are needed to establish their predictive and clinical relevance.
papers.journal: Health and quality of life outcomes

papers.title: Sleep position habits and their relationship with bruxism and temporomandibular disorder-related symptoms in adults: findings from clinical assessment and self-reported data.
papers.abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between sleep position habits and the clinical findings of bruxism and TMD-related symptoms in adult individuals. The study seeks to contribute to the understanding of bruxism and temporomandibular disorders by offering an alternative perspective on joint-related problems and supporting the development of novel approaches in clinical evaluation processes. In addition, it aims to explore the potential relationships underlying these conditions. A total of 300 individuals were included in this cross-sectional study. Data on sleep habits, the presence of tooth grinding, stress levels, physical activity, and sleep duration were collected using a structured questionnaire. All participants underwent a temporomandibular joint (TMJ) examination to assess the presence of joint pain, stiffness, and pain during function. Participants were categorized into three groups: healthy individuals, individuals with TMD-related symptoms only, and individuals with bruxism with or without accompanying TMD-related symptoms. Bruxism was assessed using subject-based information together with clinically based assessment findings, in accordance with the updated international consensus framework. No device-based assessment was performed. Questionnaire responses and clinical examination data were subjected to statistical analysis. A statistically significant difference was identified among the study groups according to sleep position (p = 0.001). Exploratory post hoc analyses suggested that the lateral sleeping position was more frequent in the Healthy group than in the Bruxism group (with or without accompanying TMD-related symptoms), whereas the combined lateral and prone sleeping position was more frequent in the Bruxism group than in the Healthy group (p < 0.05); the group with TMD-related symptoms only did not differ significantly from either group. Morning jaw pain or headache and TMJ pain or stiffness differed significantly among the groups, while pain during function was more frequent in both clinical groups than in the Healthy group (overall p < 0.001). No statistically significant differences were observed among the groups with respect to age, sex, physical activity, or sleep duration. Sleep position habits were associated with the clinical findings of bruxism and TMD-related symptoms. Although no causal or directional relationship can be inferred, the findings suggest that sleep position may represent a behavioral factor related to bruxism and TMD-related symptom patterns.

papers.title: Adjunctive transcranial direct current stimulation in super-refractory status epilepticus: a prospective case series.
papers.abstract: Super-refractory status epilepticus (SRSE) is a life-threatening neurological emergency characterized by persistent seizures despite anesthetic therapy, with high associated mortality and limited treatment options. Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) has emerged as a potential neuromodulatory intervention in refractory epilepsy; however, evidence in SRSE remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and exploratory clinical response associated with adjunctive tDCS in patients with SRSE. In this investigator-initiated prospective single-center interventional case series, 20 adult patients with convulsive SRSE admitted to a tertiary referral center between 2021 and 2025 received adjunctive cathodal tDCS (2 mA for 20 min) applied bilaterally over temporal-frontal regions while standard medical therapy was continued. Clinical and electroencephalographic (EEG) assessments were performed 30 min before and after stimulation. Feasibility and safety were primary outcomes, while short-term clinical response was assessed as an exploratory endpoint. Written informed consent for study participation and publication of anonymized clinical data and EEG recordings was obtained from legally authorized representatives prior to enrollment, and the trial was registered in the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT20230209057371N1; retrospectively registered on October 21, 2023). Four patients (20%; 95% CI: 6-44%) demonstrated short-term clinical and EEG improvement within 30 min of stimulation. No serious adverse events were observed; one patient experienced a mild, self-limited erythematous skin reaction. Hospital mortality was 50%. Exploratory subgroup differences were observed between responders and non-responders. Adjunctive tDCS was feasible and well tolerated in patients with SRSE, with short-term clinical and EEG improvement observed in a subset of patients. These preliminary findings warrant further evaluation in controlled, adequately powered studies to determine efficacy and identify predictors of response. This study was registered in the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT) under registration number IRCT20230209057371N1 on October 21, 2023. The trial was registered while participant recruitment was ongoing (retrospective registration relative to study initiation).

papers.title: Potentially inappropriate medication use among elderly Chinese outpatients in neurology clinics: a cross-sectional study comparing the beers criteria and the Chinese criteria.
papers.abstract: Older neurology outpatients may be at higher risk of potentially inappropriate medications (PIMs) due to multimorbidity and frequent use of central nervous system (CNS)-active drugs. This study assessed the prevalence of PIMs and the factors associated with PIM use among elderly neurology outpatients in China. A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted using outpatient prescription data from older outpatients attending the neurology clinic of a tertiary hospital in China between January 1 and September 30, 2025. PIMs were evaluated in parallel using the 2023 American Geriatrics Society (AGS) Beers criteria and the 2017 Chinese PIM criteria. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with PIM use, and concordance between the two criteria was assessed. A total of 5150 neurology outpatients were included. The prevalence of PIM was 44.31% according to the Beers criteria and 42.23% according to the Chinese criteria. Benzodiazepine receptor agonist hypnotics, antipsychotics, and ergoloid mesylates were the most frequently identified PIM categories under both criteria. Zolpidem was the most frequently identified PIM under the Beers criteria, whereas clopidogrel ranked first under the Chinese criteria. Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that polypharmacy, sleep disorders, and mental disorders were consistently the factors positively associated with PIM use under both criteria, whereas, atrial fibrillation and ischemic stroke showed criterion-dependent differences in their associations with PIMs. Sensitivity analyses demonstrated that these criterion-dependent differences were attributable to the divergent medication lists of the two criteria. The findings indicate a worrying prevalence of PIMs among elderly patients in neurology clinics in China. Particular attention should be paid to elderly patients prescribed benzodiazepine receptor agonist hypnotics, antipsychotics, or ergoloid mesylates, or those with risk factors such as polypharmacy, sleep disorders, and mental disorders. This study was registered at Chinese Clinical Trail Registry (Registration Number: ChiCTR2500114900).

papers.title: Isotopic red cell mass measurement: usefulness in 2026 for the diagnostic work-up of erythrocytosis.
papers.abstract: The study aimed to evaluate the role of red blood cells (RBC) isotopic mass measurement as second step in the diagnostic work-up of erythrocytosis in patients with negative initial investigations (blood gas analysis, erythropoietin [EPO] level, JAK2V617F mutation). A retrospective analysis was conducted on 93 patients who underwent RBC isotopic measurement between January 2010 and December 2022 at a tertiary care university hospital. Analysable data were available for 25 patients, of whom 20 met haemoglobin/haematocrit diagnostic thresholds for erythrocytosis and had a triple-negative initial work-up consisting of following laboratory parameters: p50/COHb, EPO levels, and JAK2V617F mutation. All patients underwent RBC isotopic measurement, with positive results defined by an increase of ≥ 25% in measured RBC volume compared to theoretical values. Among triple-negative patients (n = 20), seven (35%) presented with a positive isotopic measurement indicative of increased RBC mass. Identified causes of absolute erythrocytosis included chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, obstructive sleep apnoea, cyanotic heart disease, and neoplastic processes. Notably, 13 (65%) patients had normal RBC mass measurements, with only one patient eventually diagnosed with polycythaemia vera confirmed by bone marrow biopsy. This false negative result was caused by an undeclared therapeutic phlebotomy performed just before RBC mass analysis. As expected in relative erythrocytosis, additional investigations in the other 12 cases with a negative isotopic analysis did not yield useful diagnostic findings. Our data suggests that RBC isotopic mass measurement is a useful investigation in patients with erythrocytosis whose initial work-up does not provide diagnostic clues for either polycythaemia vera or a secondary absolute erythrocytosis. In our hands, a negative RBC isotopic measurement, along with a triple-negative initial work-up (p50/COHb, EPO level, JAK2V617F mutation) ruled out myeloproliferative neoplasia and secondary forms of absolute erythrocytosis. By utilizing RBC isotopic measurement as a second step in the evaluation of patients with erythrocytosis, unnecessary investigations can be avoided, leading to cost-effective diagnostic work-up.

papers.title: Sex-stratified associations of parenthood, child number, and youngest-child age with sexual function and psychosocial well-being.
papers.abstract: Parenthood reorganizes time, sleep, psychological load, and couple intimacy, but its sexual correlates may differ by sex and stage of child development. In this cross-sectional mixed clinic/community convenience sample, 487 married adults were included: 208 women (153 mothers, 55 childless) and 279 men (221 fathers, 58 childless). Female sexual function was assessed with a modified six-item Female Sexual Function Index score; male outcomes included the five-item International Index of Erectile Function and the Premature Ejaculation Diagnostic Tool. After multivariable adjustment, motherhood was associated with a lower modified Female Sexual Function Index score (adjusted mean difference -6.19, 95% confidence interval -8.69 to -3.69), higher Insomnia Severity Index score (8.55, 7.07 to 10.03), and lower weekly sexual frequency (-1.62, -1.99 to -1.26). Fatherhood was associated with a higher Premature Ejaculation Diagnostic Tool score (4.32, 3.16 to 5.48) and lower sexual frequency (-1.77, -2.03 to -1.51), but not with erectile-function score after adjustment. Parenthood was associated with sex-specific sexual profiles, while youngest-child age appeared more informative than child number for maternal sexual function and sleep.

papers.title: Data-driven phenotypic clustering of sleep-disordered breathing and long-term cardiovascular risk.
papers.abstract: Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) has heterogeneous cardiovascular risks that are not fully captured by the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI). We aimed to determine whether data-driven sleep-cardiometabolic phenotypes identify long-term cardiovascular risk and support phenotype-based risk stratification. We analyzed 5682 adults from the Sleep Heart Health Study baseline cohort enrolled in 1995-1998 (mean [SD] age, 63.2 [11.2] years; 52.7% female). Fifteen prespecified variables were used for k-means clustering to define SDB phenotypes. Participants with adjudicated follow-up data (n = 4909) underwent time-to-event analyses with a primary composite endpoint of various cardiovascular events. Three phenotypes were identified: Cluster 1 (aging-hypertensive OSA), Cluster 2 (healthy sleep-CVD profile), and Cluster 3 (metabolic-hypoxic OSA). Clusters 1 and 3 showed higher risks of the composite endpoint than Cluster 2 (hazard ratios [HRs], 4.06 [95% confidence interval (CI), 3.50-4.71] and 3.62 [95% CI, 2.94-4.44], respectively) and consistently elevated cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, and stroke risks. Heart failure risk was pronounced for Clusters 1 and 3 (HRs, 5.46 [95% CI, 4.41-6.76] and 5.55 [95% CI, 4.23-7.29], respectively) compared with Cluster 2. The multinomial classifier demonstrated high accuracy and discrimination in the internal test set. The phenotype-based risk score exhibited a clear stepwise gradient in predicted and observed cardiovascular risk and retained prognostic value in the external cohort, outperforming the AHI with acceptable calibration. Multidimensional phenotyping identifies SDB subgroups with divergent cardiovascular risk. A phenotype-based score using routine variables may improve risk stratification beyond event frequency alone.

papers.title: Evidence for circadian clock control of Staphylococcus aureus invasion into human lung epithelial cells.
papers.abstract: An endogenous biological clock, the circadian clock, coordinates life with the 24-hour day/night environmental cycle. In mammals, a central pacemaker in the suprachiasmatic nucleus of the hypothalamus coordinates timing between peripheral clocks and with the environment and, for example, modulates immune responses to infections. However, its role in controlling bacterial infections at a cellular level is not understood. Here, we investigate the role of the host cellular clock during infection by a highly drug-resistant human pathogen, Staphylococcus aureus. Our findings revealed that S. aureus invasion into epithelial cells was dependent on the host circadian phase. Interestingly, cells deficient in BMAL1, a transcriptional activator and an essential clock protein, demonstrated increased bacterial uptake compared to parental A549 cells. The BMAL1-knockdown (KD) cells showed significant induction of GP340, a receptor of the S. aureus adhesin, SraP. An S. aureus sraP mutant exhibited blunted rhythmic uptake into A549 cells or an increased uptake into BMAL1-KD compared to parental A549 cells. Of note, other bacterial adhesin mutants showed rhythmic and higher uptake in BMAL1-KD cells. Hence, we report that S. aureus epithelial cell invasion is clock-modulated and mediated through the S. aureus SraP-GP340 pathway, suggesting potential for host clock-directed therapy against this pathogen.

papers.title: Vibrotactile stimulation selectively enhances motor memory consolidation in adults with ADHD: A diagnosis-specific effect.
papers.abstract: Task-irrelevant sensory stimulation represents a potential non-pharmacological intervention to optimize arousal states during procedural learning; this may benefit adults with ADHD wherein arousal dysregulation may limit memory formation. Ninety-seven young adults (65 unmedicated ADHD, 32 controls; ages 19-35) were randomized to motor sequence training with or without concurrent low-intensity vibrotactile stimulation (VtSt) via a vibrating cushion. Correct sequences and errors per 30-second block were assessed across acquisition, overnight consolidation (24 h), and retention (1-week) phases. Acute VtSt effects were tested at one-week. Post-training actigraphy-derived sleep-wake parameters and chronotype (MEQ) were evaluated as consolidation-phase gain predictors. A linear mixed-effects model with Diagnosis, Condition, Wave, and Timepoint as fixed factors revealed that VtSt did not affect acquisition. A significant Diagnosis × Condition × Timepoint interaction (p = 0.006) emerged. In ADHD, VtSt selectively enhanced overnight consolidation gains (p = 0.025, Cohen's d = 0.40), with numerically superior performance maintained through 1-week (p = 0.060); acute VtSt re-presentation at 1-week enhanced performance (p = 0.020). In ADHD, consolidation gains were predicted by chronotype (β = 0.289, p = 0.024) and VtSt condition (β = 0.334, p = 0.010) but not sleep-wake parameters. Controls showed no significant VtSt effects at any re-test. When trained with VtSt, ADHD participants, but not controls, showed larger consolidation gains, sustained through 1-week retention. These findings support arousal optimization models and a precision medicine framework wherein chronotype and ADHD diagnosis may stratify individuals by intervention responsiveness and optimal timing for sensory-environmental intervention.

papers.title: Emotional challenges and coping strategies in the transition to fatherhood: perspectives of new fathers and health professionals: a qualitative study.
papers.abstract: Fathers' needs are often overlooked in perinatal care. This study explored the emotional, practical, and relational challenges of transitioning to fatherhood and identified opportunities for digital support.We interviewed expectant and new fathers and health professionals working in perinatal care. Fathers discussed their emotional experiences, daily challenges, coping strategies, and interactions with healthcare services. Health professionals described existing support and gaps in care. We used thematic analysis to identify patterns across both groups. Fathers described worry, anxiety, frustration, and helplessness associated with sleep deprivation, changing relationships, work pressures, and uncertainty about caregiving. Many felt excluded from antenatal education and unsure how to support a partner experiencing emotional distress. Mother-centred care, limited involvement in appointments, and stigma around expressing emotions made it harder for fathers to seek help. Health professionals identified gaps in support and opportunities to involve fathers more actively in perinatal care.Fathers wanted to be involved and confident in caregiving, yet uncertainty about their role, exclusion from care, and social expectations that discourage vulnerability shaped their experiences of distress. The findings highlight the need for father-inclusive perinatal care and accessible digital tools that offer practical guidance, emotional support, and opportunities for connection. Further research with more diverse groups of fathers could inform the development of equitable and responsive interventions.
papers.journal: Journal of reproductive and infant psychology

papers.title: Sleep habits, school willingness, and health-related absenteeism: a cross-sectional study of Japanese high school students.
papers.abstract: To assess the independent associations of sleep duration, chronotype, and social jetlag with school attendance motivation and health-related absenteeism among high school students. A questionnaire survey was conducted between September 2017 and January 2019 in 7 high schools in Tokyo and Saitama, Japan. Sleep duration, chronotype (mid-sleep on free days corrected for sleep debt: MSFsc), social jetlag, and sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index) were assessed. Among 2658 participants (mean age: 16.3 years; 70.7% female), 548 (20.6%) expressed unwillingness to attend school and 399 (15.0%) reported one or more absences per week. After multivariable adjustment, greater absolute social jetlag was associated with unwillingness (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 1.20, 95% CI 1.11-1.30), whereas smaller absolute social jetlag was associated with absenteeism (AOR 0.84, 95% CI 0.77-0.93). Later MSFsc was associated with absenteeism (AOR 1.24, 95% CI 1.15-1.33) but not with attendance motivation (AOR 1.01, 95% CI 0.94-1.08). Poor sleep quality was associated with both unwillingness (AOR 2.17, 95% CI 1.74-2.71) and absenteeism (AOR 1.75, 95% CI 1.34-2.28). Average sleep duration of 10 hours or more showed the largest estimate for absenteeism (AOR 5.79, 95% CI 3.06-10.95). This study demonstrated the two-sided nature of social jetlag; greater misalignment was associated with lower attendance motivation but with fewer actual absences. Poor sleep quality and late chronotype were also associated with poorer attendance. Students requiring longer sleep may represent an additional subgroup warranting attention in addressing school attendance problems.

papers.title: The effect of wearing a sleep cap on the sleep and physiological variables of infants hospitalized in the neonatal intensive care unit: A randomized controlled experimental study.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the effect of a specially designed sleep cap on the sleep and physiological variables of infants hospitalized in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). This randomized controlled experimental study included 53 infants (Intervention group: 26, Control group: 27) born after 32 weeks of gestation between September 2020 and March 2021. Infants in the intervention group wore a sleep cap developed by the investigator during sleep, while infants in the control group did not. Video recordings were taken over three consecutive days (7:00 PM and 7:00 AM) and evaluated by the investigator and an independent expert. Variables evaluated included sleep duration, number of awakenings, and physiological parameters. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, chi-square test, t-test, Mann-Whitney U test, Friedman test, Wilcoxon test, and repeated measures ANOVA. On the third follow-up day, a statistically significant increase in sleep duration was observed in the intervention group compared to the control group (p = 0.006). Although there was no significant difference in the total number of awakenings, a significant decrease in awakenings was detected, especially in premature infants (p = 0.016). In addition, significantly higher oxygen saturation levels were observed in the intervention group on the second follow-up day (p < 0.001). The use of the developed sleep cap increased sleep duration, reduced awakenings, and improved oxygen saturation levels in infants in the NICU. The use of a sleep cap may be recommended to improve sleep quality in infants hospitalized in the NICU. The research protocol was registered in the Clinical Trials with the NCT07423962.

papers.title: From population targets to personalised titration: translating within-patient electroencephalographic responses into clinical practice.
papers.abstract: Population-derived target ranges of drug concentrations or EEG indices are commonly used in clinical practice for the titration of anaesthesia. By definition, this inevitably results in a relative overdose for most patients and an underdose for a few. For accurate individualised titration of anaesthesia, suitable within-subject targets need to be established. To be reliable, these targets require a measurable EEG response to changes in the hypnotic drug concentration, an EEG endpoint that reliably indicates absence of consciousness, and stability in the EEG drug-dose response relationship so that it is not influenced by other factors that might change through the course of the operation.

papers.title: Closed-loop systems for automated hypnotic drug delivery during general anaesthesia: control performance and clinical outcomes. Response to Br J Anaesth 2026; 137: 1851-2.
