Prevalence and predictors associated with loneliness among Korean adolescents: Results from a nationally representative survey.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to identify the prevalence of loneliness and analyze its sociodemographic and health-related correlates among Korean community-dwelling adolescents. Adolescent loneliness is a critical and urgent global public health concern. Although it has been examined across different populations and settings, population-based evidence simultaneously examining a broad range of sociodemographic and health factors remains limited, particularly in non-Western sociocultural contexts. Evidence from nationally representative adolescent samples can help identify vulnerable groups and facilitate cross-cultural comparisons of factors associated with loneliness. This cross-sectional study analyzed secondary data from the 17th Korea Youth Risk Behavior Survey, comprising 54,848 adolescents (28,401 males; 26,447 females), using the Rao-Scott chi-square test and complex sample logistic regression. Loneliness prevalence among adolescents was 16.0%, with significantly high rates among female students, middle schoolers, those with COVID-19-related household economic deterioration or low household economic status, those living without family, and those who experienced violence requiring hospital treatment. Higher loneliness was also associated with smoking, alcohol consumption, using smartphones ≥5 h daily, perceiving one's health status as unhealthy, low sleep satisfaction, or perceiving one's body image as either "thin" or "fat." These findings highlight the need to evaluate both sociodemographic and health-related factors when screening adolescents. They support targeted screening and early interventions for adolescents with multiple vulnerabilities in schools and communities. Additionally, as population-level evidence from a non-Western setting, these data advances cross-cultural research on adolescent loneliness and informs future studies of culturally appropriate prevention strategies.

papers.title: Delirium Electroencephalography and Phenotyping with Endpoints (DEPEND) study: protocol for a longitudinal observational cohort study of hospitalised patients.

Cognition in 6-17-year-olds with Generalized and Focal Pharmaco-responsive Non-structural Epilepsies and its Correlates on Diffusion Tensor Imaging and Quantitative EEG: A Comparative Observational Study.
papers.abstract: The study compares cognition and its correlates on diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and quantitative electroencephalogram (qEEG) between generalized and focal pharmaco-responsive non-structural epilepsies and evaluates behavioral comorbidities. The study was conducted in a tertiary care teaching hospital in north India in 20 generalized and 30 focal pharmaco-responsive non-structural epilepsies in 6- to 17-year-olds. Cognition was tested using Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children-IV (WISC-IV) and Stroop test and behavior was evaluated using Childhood Behavior Checklist (CBCL). All the cases underwent DTI and a subset underwent resting and task-based qEEG evaluation. Cognition scores were comparable between generalized and focal epilepsies; however, both showed significant impairment compared with historical controls. On DTI, fractional anisotropy of corpus callosum (body in focal and splenium in generalized) and cingulate cortex (in both) correlated significantly with cognition scores. On resting qEEG, cognition scores correlated negatively with absolute α, δ (focal epilepsy), β and θ powers (generalized epilepsy), and positively with α and δ powers (generalized epilepsy). Performance on task-based qEEG showed negative correlation with absolute delta power in both. Impaired CBCL scores were seen in 25% generalized and 16.7% focal epilepsies. Similar correlates on DTI and qEEG for generalized and focal epilepsies highlight the effect of network model of epilepsy on cognition. The negative correlation of α and β powers with WISC-IV and Stroop scores probably indicates an underlying anxious, tensed, and inattentive state leading to impaired performance in these tests. These cases should be routinely screened for behavioral comorbidities providing a therapeutic target for cognition.

papers.title: Melatonin increases NREM sleep duration in aged rats alongside changes in choroid plexus SIRT3 and cerebrospinal fluid calcium.
papers.abstract: The relationship between age-related sleep disruption, choroid plexus (ChP) proteins, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) calcium remains unclear. Male rats aged 1, 3, and 18 months were assessed using 24-h electroencephalography/electromyography, ex vivo current-clamp recordings, calcium assays, and ChP immunoblotting. In aged rats, melatonin, melatonin plus 3-TYP, and alpha-lipoic acid were evaluated in 14-day treatment comparisons. Cortical responses to altered extracellular calcium were assessed separately. Older rats exhibited more fragmented sleep, reduced non-rapid eye movement (NREM) and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, reduced cortical and ventrolateral preoptic neuronal firing under identical recording conditions, and lower ChP sirtuin 3 (SIRT3) and combined ATP2B1/2/3 immunoreactivity. CSF calcium did not differ significantly between the 3- and 18-month-old groups. Lowering extracellular calcium increased cortical firing, whereas raising it reduced firing. Melatonin increased total and NREM sleep time, CSF and plasma calcium, and ChP SIRT3 and combined ATP2B1/2/3 immunoreactivity, without significantly changing total REM sleep. Compared with melatonin alone, 3-TYP co-treatment reduced total, NREM, and REM sleep duration and attenuated selected biochemical responses. Alpha-lipoic acid partially reproduced the melatonin-associated pattern. Within-group Pearson analyses identified positive associations between CSF calcium and total sleep time in all three age groups and all four treatment groups after Holm-Šídák adjustment. These findings show that melatonin-associated increases in total sleep time accompany changes in ChP proteins and CSF calcium in aged rats, providing a basis for testing whether the ChP-CSF interface contributes to sleep regulation.

papers.title: Environmental Enrichment and Operant Behavior: A Review of Insights from Animal Research for Clinical Applications.
papers.abstract: In recent years, environmental enrichment (EE) has increasingly been incorporated into the housing conditions of laboratory animals as it influences animal behavior and brain function. Differences in housing conditions represent a critical challenge, that potentially compromises the reproducibility of experimental results. Furthermore, findings related to EE are expected to contribute to the treatment of mental health disorders and prevention of relapse. However, a comprehensive overview of the effects of EE on operant learning, particularly on lever pressing, is currently lacking. In this review, we compiled and summarized previous studies that investigated the effects of EE on lever pressing during operant learning in rats and mice. When food served as a reward, EE influenced exploratory behavior and learning but exerted little effect on motivation to get a reward and behavioral flexibility in response to a task paradigm shift. In contrast when sucrose was used, EE suppressed motivation and, depending on the experimental model, exerted contrasting effects by either enhancing or inhibiting exploratory behavior. Finally, when addictive drugs were used, EE generally suppressed drug self-administration and relapse-related behaviors. Collectively, these findings suggest that EE modulates operant learning behavior in a manner dependent upon both the type of reward and the experimental conditions.

papers.title: Loss of P2Y6 receptor signaling reduces hyperexcitable feature manifestation in a model of temporal lobe epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Multiple forms of brain injury can increase the risk for epilepsy development. Neuroinflammation may contribute to post-injury epilepsy development risk and disease severity. The purinergic damage receptor, P2Y6R, is almost exclusively expressed by microglia in the brain and can contribute to neuroinflammatory processes when activated. In prior work inducing excitotoxic brain injury, P2Y6R activation enhances microglial pro-inflammatory cytokine production, microglial lysosome biogenesis, and CA3 hippocampal neuron phagocytosis. However, P2Y6R signaling has not been explored in the context of chronic epilepsy. We adopted the intrahippocampal kainate (IHKA) model to explore how the presence or absence of P2Y6R function impacts the severity of mesial temporal lobe epilepsy using 24/7 video EEG monitoring (single-channel hippocampal depth EEG). We first determined that P2Y6 deficiency (general knockout: P2ry6-/-) reduces acute inflammation (astrogliosis, microgliosis, and CD68 phagolysosome immunoreactivity) in the IHKA model. We then developed an integrated EEG analysis platform to automatically detect excitable network features in chronic epilepsy. Through our automated analysis platform, we discovered that P2Y6R deficiency reduces the rate of network spiking and hippocampal discharges in the IHKA model. On the other hand, generalized seizures are similar in rate and severity between genotypes. Our findings suggest that P2Y6R deficiency can reduce acute inflammation in the IHKA model and certain forms of network hyperactivity in epilepsy.

papers.title: RXFP1 alleviates chronic sleep fragmentation-induced cognitive impairment by suppressing microglia activation-mediated neuroinflammation.
papers.abstract: Chronic sleep fragmentation (CSF) poses a serious threat to physical and mental health and leads to the cognitive decline. Behavioral tests revealed that learning and memory functions were impaired in CSF mice. Transcriptomic analysis was performed on hippocampal tissues from CSF mice, and the results indicated that DEGs were predominantly enriched in CSF-related pathways including behavior, circadian rhythms, inflammation, and neuronal functions. Relaxin family peptide receptor 1 (RXFP1) gene was identified for further investigation. In the hippocampus of CSF mice, mRNA levels of RXFP1 were decreased. CSF mice receiving intrahippocampal AAV9-RXFP1 exhibited better performance in the Morris water maze and object location recognition tests RXFP1 overexpression ameliorated hippocampal damage, neuronal loss, and apoptosis in CSF mice. RXFP1 overexpression suppressed microglial activation in the hippocampal region of CSF mice, reduced the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines, and down-regulated the mRNA expression of PTGS2 and NOS2. Furthermore, iNOS expression was decreased in microglia isolated from the hippocampus of CSF mice receiving intrahippocampal AAV9-RXFP1. RXFP1 overexpression inhibited the expression of TLR4 and MyD88 in the hippocampus of CSF mice, and reduced nuclear translocation of p65 in both hippocampal tissue and microglia. RXFP1 overexpression suppressed LPS-induced activation of BV2 cells and blocked the NF-κB signaling pathway. Rescue experiments confirmed that RXFP1 modulates microglial activation via the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling cascade. The present study demonstrated that RXFP1 might alleviate cognitive impairment in CSF mice, at least in part, by suppressing microglia-associated neuroinflammation and the downstream TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling pathway.

papers.title: An open-source hardware and software platform for automated monitoring and analysis of voluntary wheel running in mice.
papers.abstract: Voluntary wheel running is a natural behaviour of laboratory mice that is widely used as environmental enrichment, as a translational model of exercise and as a marker of physiological and circadian function. Its wider use has been limited by the high cost of commercial monitoring systems and the analytical complexity of many open-source alternatives. Here, we describe and evaluate a low-cost, open-source wheel-running monitoring system built from readily available electronic components: an Arduino UNO R3 microcontroller, Hall-effect sensors and saucer-style running wheels. The hardware is coupled to the DeltaV Locomotor Analysis Platform (ΔV-LAP v0.1), a no-code software suite that automates the analysis from raw sensor recordings to locomotor measures, comparisons between animals and optional AI-generated summaries. Motor-driven bench testing at three rotation rates showed high repeatability and close agreement among the eight recording channels; agreement with an independent reference speed was not assessed. Continuous round-the-clock recording over nine days in eight adult male C57BL/6 mice showed the expected nocturnal pattern, with most running in the dark phase; after excluding one night with a lighting failure, running distance and duration did not differ significantly across days, whereas running speed increased slightly, and individual mice differed markedly in how much they ran. Distance, active duration and bout count were closely correlated with one another, as were mean and peak speed, both between and within animals. By reducing both hardware cost and analytical complexity, the system makes continuous monitoring of voluntary wheel running accessible to laboratories without engineering or programming expertise, in studies where wheel access is compatible with the experimental design.

papers.title: Differences in brain responses to letter-sound and animal-sound in Arabic-speaking children learning to read.
papers.abstract: Audio-visual integration (AVI), the ability to combine auditory and visual information, is essential for language acquisition and reading. Research on Western languages has demonstrated that tasks such as letter-sound matching are essential for developing print-sound associations and improving reading fluency. This study examined the neurobiological correlates of AVI in Arabic, using two electroencephalography (EEG) tasks: letter-sound and animal-sound congruent vs. incongruent conditions, with 63 first-grade Arabic-speaking children. Latencies and amplitudes of the N200 and P300 components were compared using an RM-ANOVA across congruent and incongruent letter-sound and animal-sound conditions. Results demonstrated significantly larger N200 amplitudes during animal-sound integration, with no significant congruency effect. In contrast, the P300 showed a robust congruency effect across stimulus categories, with a larger P300 amplitude for the incongruent condition than for the congruent condition. Importantly, greater letter-animal congruency differences in N200 latency during letter-sound processing were associated with faster rapid automatized naming, stronger naming abilities, and better working memory performance. These findings suggest that letter-specific N200 latency differentiation during audiovisual integration is associated with early processing-efficiency markers that precede fluent reading development.

papers.title: The circadian gene Nr1d1 regulates female luteinization via the NF-κB pathway.
papers.abstract: Luteinization is essential for luteal function. Progesterone secreted by the corpus luteum is critical for pregnancy. Evidence indicates that the circadian clock regulates luteinization; however, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. To investigate the effects of circadian rhythm disruption on luteinization, a constant-light-exposure mouse model was established. In vitro luteinization models using mouse ovarian granulosa cells and KGN cells were employed to investigate the specific circadian clock effector Nr1d1 and its regulatory mechanisms. In mice, constant light exposure was associated with altered expression of ovarian circadian clock genes and enhanced luteinization-associated responses. In mouse granulosa cells, Bmal1 knockdown caused circadian rhythm disturbances, reduced luteinization-related gene expression, and resulted in luteinization failure and decreased progesterone secretion. In KGN cells, the Nr1d1 agonist SR9009 promoted luteinization-related gene expression, enhanced luteinization, and increased progesterone secretion. Conversely, treatment with the Nr1d1 inhibitor SR8278 or si-Nr1d1 in KGN cells yielded opposite effects. In KGN cells, LPS-mediated activation of the NF-κB pathway induced luteinization failure and decreased progesterone secretion. In contrast, co-treatment with SR9009 and LPS reduced NF-κB pathway activity, enhanced luteinization, and increased progesterone secretion. Collectively, these findings indicate that the circadian clock gene Nr1d1 facilitates luteinization potentially through suppressing the NF-κB pathway.

papers.title: Identification of saltiness-enhancing peptides from mung bean (Vigna radiata L.) protein and their peripheral recognition and cortical response patterns.
papers.abstract: Saltiness-enhancing peptides are promising sodium-reduction ingredients, but their sensory persistence and central neural responses remain unclear. In this study, mung bean (Vigna radiata L.) protein was subjected to controlled enzymatic hydrolysis and ultrafiltration. Peptides in the UF-4 fraction were identified by LC-MS/MS and prioritized using previously reported taste-related sequence fragments and exploratory docking against ENaC, TMC4, and TRPV1. Thirty-four candidate peptides were shortlisted, and five were subsequently synthesized for validation. In 0.4% NaCl, RPFF exhibited the highest saltiness enhancement rate of 90%, followed by FDGF, APDLRGY, WDDIGGL, and AEFF. FDGF and RPFF prolonged saltiness perception for more than 45 s. EEG analysis revealed condition-dependent low-frequency responses mainly over the central and parieto-occipital scalp regions, with FDGF and RPFF exhibiting broader and more sustained patterns. These findings provide a multilevel characterization of mung bean-derived saltiness-enhancing peptides and support their potential as natural sodium-reduction ingredients.

papers.title: Unmet needs, quality of life, and lived experiences of patients with metastatic breast cancer in Central Vietnam: A convergent mixed-methods study.
papers.abstract: Metastatic breast cancer (mBC) imposes substantial burdens that compromise quality of life (QoL). While well documented in high-income countries, evidence on unmet supportive care needs and lived experiences in resource-constrained settings like Central Vietnam remains scarce. This convergent mixed-methods study enrolled 283 patients with mBC across eight hospitals in Central Vietnam. Quantitative assessments utilized the EORTC QLQ-C30, DASS-21, and the adapted Cancer Survivors' Unmet Needs scale (CaSUNE-VN). Concurrently, a purposive subsample of 38 patients completed in-depth semi-structured interviews. Survey data were analyzed using descriptive and analytical statistics, while interview transcripts underwent reflexive thematic analysis. Mean patient age was 56.3 ± 11.3 years, and 36.7% had de novo metastases. The top unmet needs were financial support (65.4%), sleep improvement (49.8%), and fear of cancer recurrence (45.2%). Global QoL was moderately impaired (mean 59.42 ± 19.13). Even with 100% health insurance coverage, financial difficulties scored highest among all symptom/item scales (60.42 ± 36.98), exceeding fatigue and pain. High rates of anxiety (66.1%) and depression (51.6%) were observed. Five core qualitative themes emerged: (1) financial toxicity as the core burden; (2) duality of the healthcare experience; (3) the family as an essential lifeline; (4) the profound psychosocial toll; and (5) redefined lives and altered perspectives. Patients with mBC in Central Vietnam experience severe financial toxicity and psychological distress. While family support buffers distress, priorities include expanding insurance coverage for targeted therapies, integrating routine distress screening, and conducting educational initiatives to dispel misconceptions surrounding early palliative care.

papers.title: Immunometabolic reprogramming links circadian cytokine signaling to flare-resolution-remission transitions in rheumatoid arthritis.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis is characterized by persistent synovial inflammation, recurrent flares, and marked daily variation in symptoms. These features reflect two related but distinct temporal dimensions: circadian regulation, which shapes the daily timing of inflammatory activity, and the flare-resolution-remission cycle, which governs changes in inflammatory burden over longer periods. Studies of human rheumatoid synovium and peripheral blood show that inflammatory stimuli can alter clock components, including brain and muscle ARNT-like 1 and period circadian regulator 2; the reciprocal effects of clock components on inflammation depend on cell type and experimental context. Metabolic abnormalities in T cells, glycolytic reprogramming in macrophages and fibroblast-like synoviocytes, hypoxia-related signaling, and metabolite-dependent chromatin regulation can shape inflammatory responses and tissue states. Histone lactylation and acetylation may participate in transcriptional regulation during active inflammation, but current evidence does not establish these marks as independent carriers of relapse susceptibility over weeks or months. More persistent susceptibility may instead involve chromatin and transcriptional states, durable reprogramming of synovial fibroblasts, tissue-resident memory T cells, and local tissue niches, although their relative contributions remain uncertain. Importantly, a relapse-prone state does not determine when a clinical flare will occur. We distinguish circadian optimization of drug administration from intervention tailored to disease phase. Randomized evidence is strongest for modified-release glucocorticoids, whereas evidence for bedtime methotrexate and nocturnal baricitinib remains limited by study design. Metabolic blockade and pro-resolving interventions remain largely preclinical. This review integrates circadian cytokine regulation, immunometabolic reprogramming, and disease-state transitions to define the evidence and translational limits of time-oriented strategies in rheumatoid arthritis.

papers.title: A scoping review to identify patient reported measurement instruments of glucocorticoid toxicity for the OMERACT Glucocorticoid Impact working group.
papers.abstract: Glucocorticoids (GCs) are commonly used in inflammatory conditions including autoimmune rheumatic diseases (AIRDs), but can cause considerable adverse effects. The Outcome Measurement in Rheumatology (OMERACT) GC Impact Working Group has developed a core domain set for measuring GC toxicity. Here, we describe work identifying existing patient reported outcome (PRO) measures, with clinician reported outcome measures (ClinROs) reported in a separate article. Medline, EMBASE, CINHAL and Cochrane Central were searched along with hand search of abstracts presented at major relevant rheumatology meetings (abstracts restricted to past 5 years (08/2019 - 08/2024) for studies referring to the use of exogenous GCs and reporting a ClinRO or PRO. Data extraction was performed in duplicate by 2 authors. 3694 individual records were identified and screened. 76 eligible studies were included for data extraction. 24 studies included a PRO. 16 of these included a validated PRO including a severity rating scale, representing 14 PROs. 6 studies (37.5%) included a patient population with AIRDs, 9 (56.3%) included non-AIRD populations and one included a mixed AIRD/non-AIRD population (6.3%). The PROs most commonly mapped to the mood disturbance (n=12), fatigue (n=8) and sleep disturbance (n=6) domains. We demonstrate the heterogeneity of instruments used to assess GC toxicity, highlighting the need for a standardised measure to adequately convey the burden of GCs on patients and allow comparison between studies. The next step will be to formally map these instruments to the core domain outcome set.

papers.title: Decoding sleep disturbances in post-traumatic stress disorder: Pathophysiology and treatment implications.
papers.abstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a chronic psychiatric disorder triggered by extreme traumatic events, with sleep disturbance being a core symptom. However, definitive conclusions regarding the specific characteristics of alterations in sleep architecture in PTSD are still lacking, and the relationship between sleep alterations at different stages of PTSD and the disease course remains unclear. This knowledge gap contributes to the absence of effective pharmacological treatments for specific symptom clusters and deficiencies in the prevention and management of PTSD itself. This review synthesizes research on sleep changes in PTSD patients, summarizes phenotypic sleep alterations in stress-related animal models, explores the differential impact of various stressors on sleep, and examines the role of sleep in regulating fear memory. We also systematically evaluate current intervention methods for PTSD-related sleep problems and the relevance of sleep disorders during the acute stress disorder (ASD) period to the subsequent development and progression of PTSD. This review aims to provide a basis for treating this core symptom, identify research gaps in the field, and uncover new therapeutic strategies for PTSD prevention and management.

papers.title: Epistaxis recurrence: Exploratory clinical prediction score from a retrospective cohort.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to identify the risk factors for epistaxis recurrence, to evaluate their association in the recurrence risk and to evaluate time to recurrence. This retrospective study included all patients admitted to our emergency department for a first episode of spontaneous epistaxis during the recruitment period between January 2022 and July 2023. Recurrence was defined as a new bleeding episode occurring at least 21 days after the initial episode. Potential risk factors were collected from medical charts and analyzed through a LASSO penalized regression. The selected variables were subsequently included in a multivariable logistic regression model and used to develop an exploratory clinical prediction score. Finally, the time to recurrence was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Among 219 patients analyzed, 68 (31.1%) experienced recurrence, of whom 80.9% recurred within 100 days. The LASSO analysis selected ten potential predictive factors: obesity, coronary artery disease, arterial hypertension, chronic kidney disease, obstructive sleep apnea, history of severe epistaxis, coagulopathy, anticoagulant medication, age over 70 and chronic alcohol use. Three factors were independently associated with epistaxis recurrence after multivariable logistic regression analysis: Chronic kidney disease 7.64 CI 95% [2.78-23.75], History of severe epistaxis 27.05 CI 95% [4.62-239.04], and Coagulopathy 7.05 CI 95% [1.67-32.44]. Three factors were found to be independently associated with epistaxis recurrence. But ten potential predictors were selected to develop an exploratory clinical prediction score but requires further validation.

papers.title: Estimating sleep apnea severity from diaphragmatic electromyography signals.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a highly prevalent sleep disorder diagnosed by polysomnography, which is a resource-intensive procedure with limited accessibility. This study proposes a non-obtrusive framework for OSA severity estimation based on diaphragmatic electromyography (dEMG) recordings from 65 patients referred for OSA evaluation during PSG-defined sleep.Approach: A higher-order singular value decomposition approach was used to simultaneously estimate electromyography (EMG) respiratory effort and electrocardiography (ECG) from four electrodes placed on the skin surface, enabling the parallel extraction of complementary physiological features. Features extracted from 30-s windows were used to train a binary XGBoost classifier that produced window-level apnea/hypopnea predictions, evaluated using the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUROC). The predictions were subsequently aggregated into patient-level severity estimates and evaluated using near-boundary double-labeling (NBL) Cohen's kappa κ. Three modality configurations were compared: ECG-only, EMG-only, and combined ECG+EMG.Main results: The combined ECG+EMG configuration achieved a window-level AUROC of 0.72 and a patient-level NBL κ of 0.484 (κ = 0.325), with a severity classification accuracy of 60%, outperforming both the ECG-only (AUROC = 0.62, NBL κ = 0.255, κ = 0.160) and EMG-only (AUROC = 0.64, NBL κ = 0.243, κ = 0.165) configurations.Significance: These findings indicate that respiratory and cardiovascular information extracted simultaneously from dEMG recordings provides complementary information for automated OSA severity estimation, supporting the potential of this non-obtrusive modality for OSA screening and motivating further evaluation in larger clinical cohorts.

papers.title: Classifying cases of Shift Work Disorder (SWD) in research: A systematic review of published approaches in human studies, with recommended reporting guidelines.
papers.abstract: Shift work disorder (SWD) is a circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder experienced by workers on schedules that overlap with their typical nocturnal sleep opportunity. Given associations of key diagnostic symptoms (insomnia and excessive sleepiness) with health and safety risks, studies have explored associations and treatment targets. However, approaches to defining SWD appear highly variable, impacting interpretation and translation of findings. We aimed to better characterize how existing studies approach SWD case determination, with a view to highlight opportunities to improve between-study consistency and translation of findings. This systematic review (CRD420250652800) identified 93 publications that determined SWD cases across intervention (n = 21), observational (n = 68) and experimental (n = 4) studies, over a 22-year period. Comprehensive evaluation of methodological approaches highlighted variability in diagnostic criteria applied, methods for evaluating individual patient presentations (e.g., clinical interviews, questionnaires, independent question items), operationalization of key SWD symptoms, inclusion and exclusion of shift schedule types, and consideration of differential diagnoses. This review highlights highly variable methodologies that may impact our understanding of prevalence and predictors of SWD, and how this understanding translates into symptom management. Transparent and consistent reporting of methodology is required, along with an increased focus on intervention trials which target broader symptom profiles to support patients with SWD.

papers.title: Dynamic mesh pattern-based substance use addiction detection from EEG signals.
papers.abstract: An explainable EEG framework is presented to distinguish participants with substance use disorder (SUD) from healthy controls. Dynamic features are extracted. The signal relations retained by the model can also be traced. In Dynamic Mesh Pattern (DynMeshPat), a path is selected within a fixed local mesh according to the signal. Five vectors and four consecutive differences are converted into channel-rank sequences and transition features. In DynMeshPat-XFE, this representation is combined with cumulative weighted neighborhood component analysis (CWNCA). The t algorithm-based k-nearest neighbors classifier (tkNN) and Directed Lobish (DLob) are also used. The analysis was based on 1985 EEG segments: 904 SUD and 1081 control. These were obtained from 60 participants: 25 with SUD and 35 controls. Leave-one-subject-out cross-validation (LOSO CV) was used. All segments from each participant were assigned to one outer test fold. Feature selection was repeated within the LOSO procedure. The 22-column model achieved 99.45% segment-level accuracy. Balanced accuracy, macro F1-score, and geometric mean were 99.43%, 99.44%, and 99.43%, respectively. The Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) was 0.989. SUD sensitivity was 99.23%, and control specificity was 99.63%. A1, A2, and E were excluded before feature extraction. Segment-level accuracy then rose to 99.70%. The selected features were described with sensor-space symbols through DLob. The reported performance is segment-level and does not establish participant-level diagnostic accuracy or a validated cortical biomarker.

papers.title: Reduced mismatch negativity to jittered frequency deviants but preserved gamma-band power in first episode psychosis.
papers.abstract: Psychotic disorders are debilitating mental health conditions that affect around 3% of the population. Traditional dopaminergic antipsychotic medications are generally effective in treating positive psychotic symptoms (such as hallucinations), however, they fail to substantially improve functioning for around 30-40% of patients, and show less efficacy for negative and cognitive symptoms. These limitations are hypothesised to result from glutamatergic system dysfunction which leads to excitation/inhibition (E/I) imbalances. Using electroencephalographic (EEG) measures relating to E/I imbalance, specifically gamma power (30-90 Hz) and mismatch negativity (MMN), may provide biomarkers for symptom severity in individuals in early psychosis. Accordingly, the primary objective of the current study was to determine how resting-state gamma power and MMN amplitude differ in individuals with a first episode of psychosis (FEP) compared to healthy controls (HC); and if these measures scale with symptom severity. To address this, we recorded 64-channel EEG data from young people (15-25 years) experiencing FEP (N = 31) and healthy controls (N = 27). During a resting-state task, we examined total gamma power, and periodic (oscillatory) and aperiodic (non-oscillatory) contributions to low (30 - 45 Hz) and high (55 - 90 Hz) gamma band power at frontal, central and posterior (Fz, Cz and Oz electrodes) locations. In addition, the MMN to frequency (pitch) and duration deviants was examined at frontal locations (Fz electrode) using a jittered interstimulus interval paradigm. Finally, we correlated the FEP group measures with their symptom severity at time of EEG collection and six weeks later. Results for gamma power showed no differences across any measures between for the FEP and HC groups. For the MMN, we found no differences in the duration MMN, however, the frequency MMN was attenuated for those with FEP. Finally, we found no significant correlations with any measures and symptom severity or psychosocial functioning. Our findings suggest that responses to frequency deviants are reduced in those with a FEP, however, this is not accompanied by changes in gamma power and does not index current or near-future symptom severity or decline in functioning.

papers.title: Clinical Characteristics of Pediatric Infection-Triggered Encephalopathy Syndrome With Bilateral Claustrum Lesions.
papers.abstract: To characterize the clinical features, cranial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings, and outcomes of pediatric infection-triggered encephalopathy syndrome (ITES) with bilateral symmetrical claustrum lesions and compare them with established ITES subtypes. We retrospectively analyzed children with ITES and bilateral symmetrical claustrum lesions admitted to the Capital Center for Children's Health from January 2016 to February 2024 and compared them with children with acute necrotizing encephalopathy and mild encephalopathy with reversible splenial lesion. Eight children with bilateral claustrum lesions were included. Clinical manifestations included seizures, psychiatric symptoms, sleep disturbances, cognitive decline, impaired consciousness, involuntary movements, and speech disturbances. Initial MRI (median, day 8 after fever onset) was normal, whereas subsequent MRI (median, day 15) demonstrated bilateral T1-isointense and T2-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery-hyperintense claustrum lesions that resolved by a median of day 59. Cerebrospinal fluid interleukin (IL)-6 and IL-8 levels were elevated in all patients (median, 773.8 and 4280.9 pg/mL, respectively). All patients received immunotherapy and developed chronic epilepsy. At the last follow-up, all had modified Rankin scale scores of 1 and had returned to normal schooling. Compared with the acute necrotizing encephalopathy and mild encephalopathy with reversible splenial lesion groups, patients with claustrum lesions exhibited distinct clinical, inflammatory, treatment, and outcome characteristics. Pediatric ITES with bilateral symmetrical claustrum lesions may represent a distinct clinical-radiological phenotype characterized by prominent psychiatric manifestations, diverse seizures, transient claustrum abnormalities, and elevated cerebrospinal fluid IL-6 and IL-8 levels. Despite chronic epilepsy, long-term functional outcomes were favorable.

papers.title: Compact SC-LIF: A factorized hybrid network for motor imagery EEG decoding.
papers.abstract: We develop a compact motor-imagery (MI) EEG decoder and examine its classification performance and computational cost. Compact SC-LIF combines factorized temporal-spatial convolutions with channel-adaptive spike-count leaky integrate-and-fire neurons. The primary BCI Competition IV 2a comparison evaluates six models using common input trials, identical training-session validation folds, equal search budgets, and three final seeds. Additional experiments examine BCI Competition IV 2b, Zhou2016, architectural components, and channel and neuron settings. Compact SC-LIF achieves 71.91 ± 12.93% subject-level accuracy and 71.72% macro-F1 with 3,508 parameters and 6.45 million dense synaptic MACs per trial. Accuracy differences from EEGNet and FBCNet are not significant; gains over corrected PLIF-SNN, Deep4Net, and ShallowFBCSPNet range from 8.24 to 10.10 percentage points (Holm-adjusted p = 0.0195). Separate fixed-protocol controls attribute a 29.0% reduction in counted operations to front-end factorization, while the matched backend comparison does not establish an independent SC-LIF accuracy gain. The decoder combines a small parameter count with competitive MI classification under a defined evaluation protocol. Its computational savings are architectural; dense synaptic counts exclude neuron-state and memory costs and do not represent measured hardware energy.

papers.title: The Coping-Mediated Symptom Model: Extending the Theory of Unpleasant Symptoms for Sleep Disturbance and Fatigue in Cardiovascular Disease.
papers.abstract: Anxiety, sleep disturbance, and fatigue co-occur in adults with cardiovascular disease and predict poor quality of life, self-care, and health care use. The Theory of Unpleasant Symptoms (TOUS) organizes these symptoms but treats coping as an antecedent, leaving the stress-to-symptom mechanism unspecified. The Coping-Mediated Symptom Model extends TOUS by repositioning appraisal-shaped coping as a mediator and adding moderation. Drawing on Lazarus and Folkman's Stress-Appraisal-Coping framework, it specifies perceived stress and anxiety as antecedents, coping quality as mediator of a latent sleep-fatigue cluster, and social support as moderator. Autonomic and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal pathways establish plausibility. Six propositions permit structural equation modeling.

papers.title: A Multilevel Investigation of the Antecedents of Employee Sleep Quality: The Effects of Role Stressors, Affective Rumination and Servant Leadership.
papers.abstract: Sleep, as a vital dimension of human well-being, is critical for the development of individuals, organisations and society. Existing literature has paid limited attention to role stressor as an antecedent of employee sleep quality. The present research explored the effects of role stressors (role overload and role conflict) on employee sleep quality and the potential mediator role of affective rumination and the potential moderating effect of servant leadership at both inter-individual level and intra-individual level by a daily dairy study (118 participants with 983 observations) and a time-lagged, three-wave study (284 employees). The results revealed that role overload and role conflict had an indirect effect on sleep quality through affective rumination both at the within-person and the between-person levels. Moreover, servant leadership was found to buffer the negative effects of role overload and role conflict on employees' affective rumination. The current findings help to illustrate the psychological mechanism underlying the association between role stressors and employee sleep quality and found servant leadership as a novel protective factor, and provide empirical evidence for designing targeted organizational interventions and management practices to promote employees' sleep and well-being.
papers.journal: Stress and health : journal of the International Society for the Investigation of Stress

papers.title: TOC1 and ELF3 are associated with distinct transcriptional responses to ER stress in Arabidopsis.
papers.abstract: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress response is essential for maintaining protein homeostasis and cellular viability under adverse environmental conditions. Although the circadian clock coordinates physiological responses to environmental cues, the contributions of individual clock components to ER stress responses remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the involvement of circadian clock genes in tunicamycin (Tm)-induced ER stress responses. Under chronic ER stress, toc1-101 exhibited increased sensitivity, whereas elf3-1 showed relative tolerance. To further characterize their early transcriptional responses, we examined gene expression following acute Tm treatment ZT16, corresponding to the end of the light period. Compared with toc1-101, elf3-1 exhibited broader induction of ER chaperone genes, with increased expression of BIP3, ERdj3b, CNX1, and PDIL, whereas toc1-101 showed induction primarily of BIP3 and ERdj3b. The mutants also differed in the expression of unfolded protein response (UPR)-associated genes: toc1-101 exhibited increased expression of BZIP60S, BZIP60U, and BZIP28, while elf3-1 showed reduced BZIP60S induction without significant changes in the other UPR-associated genes examined. Furthermore, toc1-101 showed increased expression of cell death-associated genes, including NRP1, MC8, γVPE1, and OXI1. In contrast, elf3-1 reduced expression of these genes. Together, these findings reveal that TOC1 and ELF3 contribute to ER stress outcomes by modulating the balance between adaptive proteostasis and cell death-associated responses.

papers.title: Italian Cooperative HemoAdsorption Study for Relief of Uremic Symptoms (ICHARUS): Study Protocol for a Prospective, Multicenter, Real-World Registry.
papers.abstract: Persistent uremic symptoms remain common among patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis, even when contemporary dialysis prescriptions are optimized. These symptoms are only partially captured by conventional adequacy metrics and represent a major determinant of health-related quality of life. A growing body of evidence suggests that incomplete removal of protein-bound uremic toxins and larger middle molecules contributes to persistent symptom burden. Hemoadsorption, when integrated into the extracorporeal circuit, provides an additional clearance mechanism that may enhance solute removal beyond diffusion and convection alone. The Italian Cooperative HemoAdsorption Study for Relief of Uremic Symptoms (ICHARUS) study is a prospective, multicenter, observational, real-world registry enrolling adult patients receiving hemodialysis with persistent uremic symptoms despite optimized conventional therapy. Hemoadsorption combined with hemodialysis will be prescribed according to routine clinical practice. Study visits are scheduled at baseline and at 1, 3, and 6 months. The primary endpoint is the change in patient-reported symptom burden, assessed using the Dialysis Symptom Index, from baseline to 3 months. Secondary endpoints include changes in symptom-specific patient-reported outcomes, health-related quality of life, selected biochemical markers, and safety. By focusing on patient-reported outcomes in a pragmatic setting, the ICHARUS study aims to generate structured real-world evidence on the feasibility, safety, and potential clinical relevance of hemoadsorption combined with hemodialysis, supporting patient phenotyping and informing future hypothesis-driven interventional studies. NCT07522008.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in epilepsy fellowship training: Aligning emerging technologies with ACGME competency-based education.
Exploratory Assessment of Montelukast Sodium Oral Soluble Film on Perioperative Respiratory Adverse Events in Preschool Children: A Prospective, Single-Arm Clinical Trial.
papers.abstract: Perioperative respiratory adverse events (PRAEs) are common in preschool children undergoing general anesthesia, especially those with airway high-risk factors. Current prophylaxis with inhaled corticosteroids has limitations. Montelukast sodium oral soluble film (OSF) offers a child-friendly alternative, but its prophylactic role remains unexplored. The aim of this study was to explore the incidence of PRAEs, feasibility, and short-term safety of preoperative montelukast sodium OSF in preschool children at high risk for PRAEs. This prospective single-arm trial enrolled 212 children (aged 3-6 years) with one or more airway risk factor, scheduled for elective non-cardiac/non-thoracic surgery. Montelukast sodium OSF was given 24 h and 2 h preoperatively. Primary outcome was composite PRAE incidence from induction to 24 h postoperatively, compared with a historical benchmark of 35%. Secondary outcomes included individual PRAE subtypes, postoperative pain, emergence delirium, neuropsychiatric adverse events (NPAEs), and preoperative-to-postoperative changes in anxiety, socio-emotional symptoms, sleep habits, and health-related quality of life. Composite PRAE incidence was 24.1% (51/212), compared with a historical benchmark of 35% (absolute difference 10.9 percentage points; relative difference 31.1%; p < 0.001 for the exploratory comparison). Desaturation (17.0%) and severe coughing (10.8%) were most frequent. Subgroup heterogeneity was seen by surgical site (p = 0.004) and risk-factor count (p = 0.005). Transient postoperative neuropsychological changes resolved by 4-8 weeks; no grade ≥ 3 NPAEs occurred. In this exploratory single-arm study, preoperative montelukast sodium OSF was associated with a lower-than-expected incidence of PRAEs in high-risk preschool children. However, because of the single-arm design and the use of a historical benchmark, these findings are preliminary and hypothesis-generating only and do not establish prophylactic efficacy. Randomized controlled trials with concurrent controls are required to confirm or refute any potential effect. ChiCTR2500108403. The date of registration: 08/29/2025.

papers.title: Sleep disturbance, pain, anxiety, distress, fatigue, and functional impairment in patients with breast cancer.
papers.abstract: SPPADE symptoms (Sleep disturbance, Pain, Physical function impairment, Anxiety, Depression/distress, and Energy deficit/fatigue) may result from cancer and its treatment. The aim of this analysis was to characterize SPPADE symptoms in patients with stage 1-4 breast cancer. SPPADE data came from the Enhanced, EHR-facilitated Cancer Symptom Control (E2C2) study, a pragmatic cluster-randomized trial designed to evaluate a symptom management intervention in routine practice (Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03892967. Registered March 25, 2019). Symptom severity was measured on a 0-10 scale via an investigator-developed survey administered by patient portal, in-clinic tablet, or interactive voice response (phone) in association with an outpatient oncology encounter. Scores of 4-6 were categorized as "moderate" and ≥ 7 as "severe." In this analysis, only data from each patient's initial survey were included. A total of 9,209 patients with breast cancer completed an initial E2C2 survey between March 2019 and January 2023. The proportion with moderate or severe SPPADE symptoms was: 23% moderate and 10% severe for sleep disturbance; 17% moderate and 7% severe for pain; 19% moderate and 8% severe for anxiety; 16% moderate and 6% severe for emotional distress; 26% moderate and 12% severe for fatigue; and 21% moderate and 8% severe for impaired physical function. Younger age, non-White race, being unmarried, being unemployed or having a disability, and more education were associated with greater overall symptom burden. SPPADE symptoms are common in patients with breast cancer, especially in those who are young, non-White, unmarried, unemployed, and more educated. Routine implementation of symptom surveillance and management of these modifiable symptoms is warranted in breast oncology.

papers.title: Sleep in progressive supranuclear palsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis of polysomnographic findings.
papers.abstract: To evaluate polysomnographic measured sleep changes in patients with progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) compared with controls. MEDLINE, EMBASE, All EBM databases, and Web of Science were searched. Eight studies were included in the quantitative meta-analysis, involving 183 individuals with PSP and 158 controls. Meta-analyses revealed reduced sleep efficiency, total sleep time, and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep percentage, and increased wake time after sleep onset, N1 sleep percentage, REM latency, and apnea hypopnea index in PSP patients compared with controls. No significant group differences were observed in sleep latency, N2 sleep percentage, N3 sleep percentage, or arousal index. Our meta-analysis found that multiple objective sleep abnormalities are present in individuals with PSP compared with controls. This suggests the potential value of polysomnography in characterizing sleep disturbances in PSP. These findings might be useful for distinguishing PSP from other neurodegenerative diseases. Future research should explore the effects of clinical characteristics (i.e., disease duration, disease severity, and comorbid sleep disorders) on sleep in PSP.

papers.title: Identifying GAN mutations in three families with giant axonal neuropathy: a clinical study and literature review.
papers.abstract: Giant Axonal Neuropathy (GAN) is a very rare autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disease caused by mutations in the GAN gene encoding gigaxonin protein. Mutation in the GAN gene causes dysfunction in gigaxonin protein leading to abnormal accumulation of neurofilaments causing sensory and motor dysfunctions. The present article highlights the clinical profile, electrophysiology, and genetics of six patients belonging to three unrelated Indian families having Giant Axonal Neuropathy. These cases had an average age of onset of 5.17 years with symptoms such as progressive gait disturbance, distal muscle weakness, and recurrent falls. Prominent clinical features included nystagmus, foot deformities. Kinky hair, which is a characteristic finding was absent in all of our patients. Neurophysiologically, these patients showed signs of severe sensory and motor axonal polyneuropathy with significant reduction in mean CMAP amplitude (1.48mV) and motor nerve conduction velocity (37.17m/s). MRI scan showed typical neuroimaging findings of symmetrical diffuse deep white matter hyperintensity with sparing of the U-fibers along with severe cervical cord atrophy. Genetically, we reported three homozygous variants such as novel missense mutation (p.Tyr347Cys) in Family 1, novel 3' splice site proximal mutation (c.1237-3 C > G) in Family 2, and large (~ 76.37 KB) deletion of GAN and BCO1 in Family 3. The identification of these novel mutations expands the known genetic spectrum of GAN. Early diagnosis through integrated neuroimaging and genetic testing is crucial for effective clinical management and genetic counseling to prevent recurrence in affected families.

papers.title: Understanding psychosis in patients with epilepsy: Insights into demographic, clinical, and treatment-related factors.
papers.abstract: Although psychosis affects 2%-7% of patients with epilepsy (PWE), its mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to identify clinical, demographic, electrophysiological, and radiological factors associated with psychosis by comparing PWE with and without psychosis. Medical records of PWE were retrospectively reviewed. The case group (n = 42) comprised PWE with a psychosis, while controls (n = 84) included PWE without psychiatric comorbidity. Demographic, clinical, EEG, and neuroimaging variables were compared between the groups. Factors associated with psychosis in epilepsy were evaluated using univariate and multivariate logistic regression models, with the final multivariate model incorporating clinically relevant and univariately significant variables. Interictal psychosis was the predominant subtype (57.1%), followed by postictal and ictal psychosis. Univariate analysis showed that lower education, unemployment, longer epilepsy duration, higher number of ASMs, history of status epilepticus (SE), increased seizure frequency, poor adherence, cognitive and neurological abnormalities, background EEG slowing, and hippocampal sclerosis (HS) were significantly associated with psychosis. In the multivariate analysis, higher seizure frequency (OR = 15.31, 95% CI: 5.49-42.72; p < .001), and HS (OR = 3.81, 95% CI: 1.06-13.63; p = .04) remained statistically associated with psychosis. Psychosis in epilepsy was associated with a history of SE, higher seizure frequency, poor treatment adherence, and HS in PWE. These findings highlight potentially important clinical associations; however, the retrospective design suggests caution in drawing causal inferences. Early identification of high-risk patients and multidisciplinary collaboration may help optimize patient outcomes and improve clinical management.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape

papers.title: Efficacy of a 12-week chronotype-aligned diet versus a standard hypocaloric diet in overweight and obese women: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Aligning meal timing with individual chronotype may improve the effectiveness of hypocaloric diets. In this randomized trial, 76 women aged 19-53 years with overweight or obesity were stratified by chronotype using the Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire and randomized to a chronotype-aligned or a standard hypocaloric diet with identical energy and macronutrient content for 12 weeks. Anthropometric, body composition, biochemical, and cardiac assessments were performed at baseline and Week 12. Sixty-two completers were analyzed per protocol. Compared with the standard diet, the chronotype-aligned diet produced a greater reduction in body weight, the primary outcome (baseline-adjusted difference -2.83 kg; 95% CI -4.18 to -1.48), and greater reductions in body mass index, body fat percentage, and waist circumference. Overall baseline-adjusted differences in glycemic and lipid markers were not significant; LDL-C decreased more with the chronotype-aligned diet only in the morningness stratum (p = 0.015). Reductions in the Visceral Adiposity Index and Lipid Accumulation Product, both of which incorporate waist circumference, were greater with the chronotype-aligned diet. Cardiac parameters showed no consistent changes. A chronotype-aligned hypocaloric diet may enhance weight loss in women with overweight or obesity; larger, longer trials are needed to confirm these findings and assess long-term safety.

papers.title: EEG morphology and peri-ictal MRI abnormalities in status epilepticus and ictal-interictal continuum.
papers.abstract: Status epilepticus (SE) is a neurological emergency that may have long-term consequences. Peri-ictal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) abnormalities (PMAs) may serve as marker of potential acute ictal brain injury and can be used for estimating the risk of SE-defining electroencephalography (EEG) patterns. We hypothesized that excitatory-predominant EEG morphologies reflect higher metabolic demand and a greater likelihood of PMAs than inhibitory-predominant morphologies. In this single-center prospective cohort (February 2019-April 2025), we included patients who had either SE or ictal-interictal continuum (IIC) reported on EEG and underwent acute magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) (≤48 h). Excitatory-predominant morphology was defined by a sharp-wave amplitude greater than those of the positive and slow wave, a broad sharp wave (>200 ms), or superimposed fast activity. Inhibitory-predominant morphology was defined by the positive or slow-wave amplitude greater than that of a sharp wave. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated the association between EEG morphology and PMAs on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) or fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR). Kendall's tau and Spearman's rho assessed correlations between the number of excitatory features (0-2) and MRI sequences showing PMAs (none, arterial spin labeling [ASL] hyperperfusion only, or DWI/FLAIR). Among 205 included patients (134 IIC, 71 SE), excitatory-predominant patterns and lateralized periodic discharges were associated with increased risk of DWI/FLAIR PMAs (p = .001 and p = .02, respectively). In IIC patients, excitatory-predominant morphology was the only predictor of PMAs (p = .002). In the subset with ASL, DWI, and FLAIR sequences (n = 145), the number of excitatory features correlated strongly with types of sequences affected by PMAs (Kendall's tau p < .001; Spearman's rho p < .001). Excitatory-predominant morphology, as opposed to inhibitory-predominant patterns, was associated with a more frequent occurrence of PMAs. These findings support an EEG morphology framework based on excitatory-inhibitory balance across IIC and SE.

papers.title: Chrono-Therapeutics in Type 2 Diabetes: Translational Perspectives Using Continuous Glucose Monitoring for Integrated Optimization of Pharmacological, Nutritional, and Lifestyle Interventions.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a multisystem endocrine disorder that requires multidisciplinary management in solving its global health challenge, as its prevalence increases despite the scientific advances in therapeutic and dietary interventions. The management strategies are expected to be personalized rather than "one-size-fits-all", as their efficacy has declined over time. This occurred because of the often-overlooked significance of circadian rhythms, despite their physiological roles in energy balance, endocrine, and β-cell function. The misalignment of pharmaceutical interventions, nutrition, and lifestyle with the biological clock contributes to and complicates T2DM. The advent of Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has now enabled comprehensive assessment of glycemic variability over a long period, allowing monitoring of the impact of nutrition, physical activity, and therapy. CGM has been shown to improve the precision of therapeutic interventions in alignment with the physiological clock. This will potentially enhance efficacy, minimize adverse effects, and improve long-term metabolic outcomes. However, several articles have separately explored chronotherapeutic, chrononutrition, and lifestyle modification for T2DM management, without a clinically integrated framework. This review, from a translational perspective, integrates circadian rhythms, chronotherapeutic interventions, chronotyping, lifestyle factors, and gene variants associated with glycemic dysregulation to optimize T2DM management. A CGM-assisted multilayered chronotherapeutic algorithm was further proposed to support more personalized T2DM management and to guide prospective clinical validation and hypothesis-driven research.

papers.title: Ambulatory CPAP initiation in severe OSAS leads to lower rates of treatment withdrawal and similar patient-reported outcomes compared to in-laboratory titration: a Belgian observational study.
papers.abstract: In the context of Belgian updates to the current obstructive sleep apnea (syndrome) (OSA(S)) treatment convention, the purpose of this observational real-world study was to compare 3-month patient-reported outcomes (PROs) in OSAS patients undergoing an 'in-lab' or 'ambulatory' continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) titration pathway. Consecutive uncomplicated severe OSAS (apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) ≥30) were prospectively included. Patients were all eligible to undergo in-lab manual titration polysomnography (PSG) or ambulatory titration respiratory polygraphy (RP) under fixed CPAP (7 to 9 cm H20), in cases where they were compliant during the first 15 days of use. If not, they were moved to the 'in-lab' pathway. Clinical outcomes (PRO (questionnaires), CPAP pressure, compliance, RREs) were assessed 3 months after CPAP titration in both groups. A total of 317 severe OSAS patients were included (134 in the 'ambulatory' pathway, of whom 11% could not adapt to CPAP). PROs and compliance were similar in both groups but CPAP pressure, RREs, and withdrawal rates were significantly increased in the 'in-lab' group. The 'in-lab' group had more severe OSA characteristics at baseline and included difficult-to-treat patients from the 'ambulatory' group after CPAP adaptation failure. The closer monitoring of the 'ambulatory' group could also explain the differences. In this single-center observational study of uncomplicated severe OSAS, ambulatory CPAP management was associated with lower withdrawal rates and equivalent PROs compared to in-lab titration. These findings support the feasibility of broadening the ambulatory pathway, provided very close TMg-based follow-up is implemented from treatment initiation. Generalization to moderate or complicated OSA populations requires dedicated studies.

papers.title: Theoretical Study of Rovibronic Spectra of the Si2 Molecule.
papers.abstract: Accurate rovibronic spectra of the Si2 molecule were constructed using the DUO program, based on high-level potential energy curves and electric dipole moment data obtained at the MRCI+Q (multireference configuration interaction with Davidson correction) level employing the aug-cc-pVQZ-DK all-electron basis set. Absorption spectra spanning a wide temperature and broad wavenumber ranges are further derived within the ExoMol framework via the ExoCross program. Spectral analysis reveals that high-temperature conditions substantially extend the effective absorption range and activate high-energy transition channels, thereby modulating the overall spectral response of Si2. Comparison with the measured H3Σu- ← X3Σg- (2,0) spectrum provides a qualitative assessment of the calculated contour and reveals limitations in the reproduction of resolved fine structure and individual line positions. Full rovibronic structures of the K3Σu- ← X3Σg-(1,0) ladder and newly assigned 33Σu- ← X3Σg- (0,0), (0,1), and (1,0) bands are simulated at room temperature 298 K, compensating for the deficiencies of previous experimental measurements, which resolved only the band heads without complete rotational profiles. Quantitative comparison of spectral features and transition energies unambiguously distinguishes the literature-reported N3Σu- state from the newly identified triplet state (33Σu-), thus resolving the long-standing confusion in the assignment of the ultraviolet triplet excited state series of Si2. The high-precision spectroscopic and thermodynamic benchmark data established herein provide a robust fundamental support for refined theoretical calculations, astronomical spectral identification, and in situ plasma diagnostics of silicon-bearing molecules.

papers.title: High Prevalence of Weight-Related Comorbidities and Applicability of Screening Criteria Among Children With Overweight but Without Obesity: Insights From a Dutch Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Current guidelines recommend assessing comorbidities in children with overweight, but without obesity only when specific risk factors are present. Data on the prevalence of comorbidities in this group remain limited. Weight-related comorbidities (Type 2 diabetes, dyslipidaemia, hypertension, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome and depressive symptoms) and precursors (elevated blood pressure and insulin resistance) were assessed in 102 children with overweight but without obesity. Risk factors frequently cited in international guidelines as screening criteria were evaluated. Children (55.9% girls) had a mean age of 11.9 years (SD 2.6; range, 3.5-16.7 years) and a mean BMI z-score was 2.4 (0.3 SD). Comorbidities were identified in 66.7% of the children, and two or more comorbidities were present in 33.3%. Dyslipidaemia (35.3%), impaired liver parameters (33.3%) and hypertension (24.0%) were most prevalent. Prediabetes was observed in 7.8%, and indications of obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome in 8.5% and depressive symptoms in 5.7%. Children with comorbidities had a significantly higher waist circumference z-score than those without. Common screening criteria were met by 80.6% of the children with dyslipidemia, 50.0% with prediabetes, 41.2% with impaired liver parameters and 26.5% of children without comorbidities. The majority of children with overweight, but without obesity, had comorbidities. Common screening criteria appear insufficient to accurately identify these children, suggesting current criteria may not fully capture true risk profiles.

papers.title: Visual function and circadian rest-activity rhythms in US older adults: The National Health and Aging Trends Study.
papers.abstract: To evaluate associations of visual function with accelerometer-derived rest-activity rhythm (RAR) metrics and 24-hour continuous activity patterns among older adults. We analyzed data from 728 U.S. Medicare beneficiaries (weighted mean age 79.1±6.0 years, 78% White, 56% female) who completed objective vision assessments and provided ≥ 3 days of accelerometer data in NHATS Round 11 (2021). Visual functions included distance acuity, near acuity, and contrast sensitivity. Wrist-worn accelerometer data were used to derive parametric RAR metrics (amplitude, mesor, acrophase, alpha, beta, and percent rhythm) and nonparametric RAR metrics (relative amplitude, intradaily variability [IV], interdaily stability [IS]). Associations were examined using weighted linear regression and function-on-scalar regression (FOSR). Poorer visual function, regardless of type, was associated with lower amplitude (rhythm strength, both parametric and non-parametric metrics) and lower percent rhythm (rhythmicity), but not with mesor (average activity level), acrophase (peak activity timing), or alpha (peak-trough width). Distance acuity showed a statistically significant nonlinear association with IS. We did not observe any statistically significant associations for beta and IV after type 1 error correction. FOSR showed lower daytime activity and higher nighttime activity during typical sleep hours among those with vision impairment, with simultaneous significance limited to a small portion of the day. Findings were robust across sensitivity analyses. Worse visual function was associated with weaker and less robust circadian RARs in a representative sample of older adults. Longitudinal and mechanistic studies are warranted to understand the intertwined relationships between visual function and circadian health.
