papers.title: A Previously Unreported POU3F3 p.(Lys409Ter) Variant in Snijders Blok-Fisher Syndrome: Mechanistic Context of Expressed Truncating Alleles.
papers.abstract: Background: Snijders Blok-Fisher syndrome (SNIBFIS; OMIM #618604) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder associated with heterozygous POU3F3 variants and characterized by developmental delay, prominent speech and language impairment, behavioral abnormalities, and dysmorphic features. Case Presentation: We report a Chinese boy evaluated at 7 years and 9 months for longstanding developmental and language delay. He walked independently at 18 months, began using meaningful single words at approximately 24 months, and remained unable to produce complete sentences at 7 years of age. Wechsler intelligence testing yielded a full-scale IQ of 57. Clinical evaluation documented attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and autism spectrum disorder, with a Childhood Autism Rating Scale score of 38. Additional findings included sleep-onset difficulty, low-set ears, an open-mouth appearance, a single transverse palmar crease, and left hyperopia. He had no history of seizures, and electroencephalography was normal. Trio whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous POU3F3 nonsense variant, NM_006236.3:c.1225A>T [p.(Lys409Ter)], absent from both parental blood samples and reported as de novo by the diagnostic laboratory. The variant was not identified in the published literature or publicly accessible variant resources searched through 8 September 2026. Conclusions: This case adds to the reported POU3F3 variant spectrum and illustrates the importance of considering the unusual behavior of truncating alleles in this intronless gene.

papers.title: A Digitally Supported Hybrid Exercise and Health Education Program for Textile Workers with Musculoskeletal Disorders: A Single-Arm Pre-Post Intervention Study.
papers.abstract: Work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) are prevalent in physically demanding occupations and can impair health, functional capacity and work productivity. Textile workers face occupational risk factors, yet workplace-based interventions remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate changes in health and work-related outcomes following a hybrid intervention among textile workers with WMSDs. A quasi-experimental single-arm pre-post study with a 1-month follow-up was conducted among textile workers in Zaragoza, Spain. The 9-week intervention combined eight onsite health education workshops with an individualized, digitally supported home-based exercise program delivered via RehBody. Participants completed two weekly exercise sessions, remotely monitored by health professionals. Outcomes were assessed at baseline, postintervention, and at 1-month follow-up. Musculoskeletal pain intensity was the primary outcome; secondary outcomes included musculoskeletal symptoms, physical function, physical activity, work ability, sleep quality, psychological distress, health-related quality of life, and work productivity. Changes over time were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA or Friedman tests, as appropriate. Thirty-one participants completed all assessments (retention rate 79.5%). Musculoskeletal pain decreased significantly after the intervention and remained lower at follow-up (p < 0.01; Kendall W = 0.314). Significant improvements were observed in lower-limb functional capacity (p < 0.001; η2p = 0.773), work ability (p = 0.002; W = 0.195), and sleep quality (p = 0.004; η2p = 0.177). Seven-day shoulder symptoms and presenteeism also improved significantly (p = 0.013 and p = 0.047, respectively). Workshop attendance was 88.7%, while 69.6% of prescribed digital exercise sessions were completed. The hybrid workplace intervention was associated with improvements in musculoskeletal pain, physical function, work ability, and sleep quality. However, the uncontrolled design limits causal inferences. Larger controlled studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings and assess their long-term sustainability.

papers.title: Profiles and Factors Associated with Intrinsic Capacity Impairment in Community-Dwelling Older Adults with Cardiometabolic Diseases: A Latent Class Analysis.
papers.abstract: Background: Cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs) are highly prevalent and contribute to functional decline. Intrinsic capacity (IC) is central to healthy ageing, yet evidence on IC impairment among older adults with CMDs in under-resourced regions remains limited. This study aimed to identify distinct IC impairment profiles and associated factors among community-dwelling older adults with CMDs in the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps (XPCC), China. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 813 older adults (≥60 years) with CMDs from three urban and two rural communities within the XPCC. IC was assessed across six domains: cognition, locomotion, vitality, psychology, vision, and hearing. Latent class analysis (LCA) identified distinct IC impairment profiles, and multinomial logistic regression examined factors associated with class membership. Results: Mean age was 79.11 years (SD = 6.2), and 66.5% were female. IC impairment was nearly universal (99.2%). Psychological impairment was more prevalent among those with cardiometabolic multimorbidity (40.94% vs. 28.09%, p = 0.002). LCA identified three subgroups: "Cognition impairment" (25.34%), "Vitality-Cognition-Locomotion" (24.97%), and "Multidomain IC impairment" (49.69%). Older age, single marital status, lower education, poor self-rated health, insufficient physical activity, and poor sleep quality were significantly associated with more severe IC impairment. Conclusions: IC impairment is highly prevalent and heterogeneous among community-dwelling older adults with CMDs. These findings support a shift from disease-centred to function-centred care, with risk-stratified, personalised interventions to promote healthy ageing.

papers.title: Sitting Time in Late Pregnancy and Maternal and Neonatal Outcomes in Women with and Without Chronic Diseases: A Matched Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sedentary behavior increases in late pregnancy, but its relationship with perinatal outcomes, particularly in women with chronic diseases, is unclear. This study examined the associations of daily sitting time (ST) with sleep quality, labor and neonatal outcomes in healthy pregnant (HP) women and pregnant women with chronic diseases (CDP). Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 102 women who delivered vaginally at 36-42 weeks of gestation were included: 51 CDP and 51 HP individually matched for ST. ST was assessed with the International Physical Activity Questionnaire-Short Form and analyzed continuously and dichotomized at the median (300 min/day). Sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, PSQI), labor and neonatal outcomes were obtained from questionnaires and medical records; all outcomes were considered exploratory. Data were analyzed with matched-pairs ANCOVA adjusted for age, gestational weight change and gravidity. Results: Neonates of mothers with long ST had lower hemoglobin than those of mothers with short ST (adjusted difference -0.93 g/dL, 95% CI -1.54 to -0.32; p = 0.003, ηp2 = 0.175; not significant after Holm-Bonferroni correction, p = 0.051), with no ST × health status interaction; ST correlated inversely with neonatal hemoglobin in both HP (r = -0.45) and CDP (r = -0.32). Longer ST predicted greater maternal daytime dysfunction (β = 0.38, p = 0.006), although the dichotomized ST groups did not differ. ST was not associated with labor duration, induction, episiotomy, perineal laceration or neonatal anthropometry. Independently of ST, CDP had poorer global PSQI scores, longer sleep latency, greater daytime dysfunction and a longer active phase of labor, and their neonates had higher birth weight and 1-min Apgar scores; only the differences in daytime dysfunction and Apgar score remained significant after correction. Conclusions: Longer sitting in late pregnancy was associated with lower neonatal hemoglobin and greater maternal daytime dysfunction. These exploratory, hypothesis-generating associations do not establish causality and require confirmation in prospective studies using device-based measures of sedentary behavior and data on key determinants of neonatal hemoglobin.

papers.title: Positive Screening for Sleep-Related Breathing Disorders Among Children in Jordan: A Cross-Sectional Survey of Parents.
papers.abstract: Background: Sleep-related breathing disorders (SRBDs) in children range from primary snoring to obstructive sleep apnea and can affect health, behavior and learning. This study aimed to estimate the proportion of children in Jordan who screen positive for SRBD and to identify associated factors. Methods: This was a cross-sectional survey study that was conducted in Jordan between 27 November and 15 December 2025. Parents completed the Arabic 22-item Pediatric Sleep Questionnaire (PSQ) scale online (using Google Forms). The primary analysis was restricted to parents who reported a single child age group (one year or older) and a single mode of delivery, so that answers most likely referred to one child. A positive screen was defined as eight or more "yes" responses. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify associated factors. Results: Of 1112 respondents, 476 met the criteria and were included in the primary analysis. Among them, parent reports for 108 children (22.7%; 95% confidence interval (CI): 19.2-26.7%) screened positive for SRBD. Habitual snoring was reported for 13.7% of children and witnessed breathing pauses for 10.9%. In the multivariable regression model, a positive screen was associated with a family history of snoring or sleep apnea (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 3.72, 95% CI: 2.07-6.71), sleeping in a noisy or shared room (aOR = 2.45, 95% CI: 1.38-4.33), and having a divorced (aOR = 2.97, 95% CI: 1.17-7.56) or widowed parent (aOR = 3.83, 95% CI: 1.04-14.16). Conclusions: About one in five parent reports in this online convenience sample met the PSQ screening threshold for SRBD symptoms. A positive screen indicates a need for further evaluation and does not confirm a sleep disorder. Asking about family history of snoring and the sleep environment may help primary care and school health staff identify children who need referral for sleep assessment.

papers.title: Protocol for a Double-Blind Randomized Pilot Trial on the Augmentative Effect of Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation Combined with Maintenance Medication in Adolescents with Major Depressive Disorder.
papers.abstract: Background: Adolescent major depressive disorder (MDD) is associated with substantial functional impairment and represents a major public health concern. Although pharmacotherapy and psychotherapy are established treatments, a considerable proportion of adolescents experience inadequate treatment response, adverse effects, or poor adherence. Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) is an emerging non-invasive neuromodulation approach with potential therapeutic benefits; however, its feasibility, safety, and preliminary clinical effects in adolescents with MDD remain insufficiently investigated. This study will evaluate the feasibility, safety, and preliminary clinical outcomes of adjunctive tACS treatment in adolescents with MDD. Methods: This randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled pilot trial will enroll 30 adolescents aged 12-18 years with MDD, who will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive active or sham stimulation. Participants will undergo a 4-week intervention phase consisting of 20 stimulation sessions, followed by a 12-week follow-up phase, resulting in a total study duration of 16 weeks. Feasibility outcomes will include recruitment performance, treatment completion, and participant retention throughout the study period. Safety will be evaluated through systematic monitoring and recording of adverse events and serious adverse events. Exploratory clinical outcomes will include CDRS-R-defined response and remission, as well as changes in depressive symptoms, anxiety, suicidality, sleep quality, Clinical Global Impression scores, rumination, and health-related quality of life. Exploratory assessments will examine cognitive, neurophysiological, and behavioral changes associated with tACS treatment. Discussion: This pilot trial will provide preliminary evidence regarding the feasibility, acceptability, and safety of adjunctive tACS treatment for adolescents with MDD. The findings will help estimate potential clinical effects and inform the design of a future adequately powered randomized controlled trial.

papers.title: Music During Electronic Fetal Monitoring in Healthy Pregnancies: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Non-reactive non-stress tests (NSTs) in healthy pregnancies are often caused by fetal sleep rather than by fetal compromise, and music has been proposed as a simple means of increasing fetal reactivity. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether listening to music during electronic fetal monitoring changes fetal movements, baseline fetal heart rate (FHR), FHR accelerations and NST reactivity in healthy pregnant women. Methods: The review followed PRISMA 2020 and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024481527). Four databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus and ScienceDirect) were searched from inception to June 2024 (date of last search) for randomized, quasi-randomized, non-randomized or crossover-controlled studies, published in English or Turkish, comparing music during fetal monitoring with no music. Methodological quality was appraised with the JBI tools and the certainty of evidence with GRADE. Random-effects (restricted maximum likelihood) meta-analyses used Hedges' g, mean differences (MD) and risk ratios (RR); the primary analyses were restricted to uncomplicated pregnancies and were stratified by study design. Results: Twelve studies (1747 women) were included; eight contributed to the primary meta-analyses, three were used in sensitivity analyses only, and one was synthesized narratively. Music-mostly slow-tempo classical, instrumental or culturally familiar pieces, self-selected by the woman in four studies and delivered through headphones or a personal player for 10-30 min with playback volume adjusted for comfort where reported-increased fetal movements (6 studies, n = 549; g = 0.69, 95% CI 0.30-1.07; I2 = 74%) and FHR accelerations (7 studies, n = 688; g = 0.60, 95% CI 0.24-0.97; I2 = 78%) and modestly increased the proportion of reactive NSTs (5 studies, n = 687; RR = 1.29, 95% CI 1.04-1.59; I2 = 90%), without changing baseline FHR (8 studies, n = 909; MD = 1.3 bpm, 95% CI -0.5 to 3.2). Heterogeneity was high, prediction intervals included no effect, the reactivity effect was not robust to the Hartung-Knapp adjustment or to restriction to randomized trials, and the certainty of evidence was low (very low for reactivity). Conclusions: Music during the NST is a promising, low-risk adjunct that may increase fetal activity and accelerations without altering baseline FHR, but the evidence comes from small, heterogeneous and partly non-randomized studies identified in four databases and two languages; one study reported a shorter time to a reactive result with music, but no study assessed total test duration, downstream clinical management (repeat testing, additional investigations) or perinatal outcomes. Adequately powered randomized trials with standardized music protocols are needed before music can be recommended for routine use.

papers.title: Economic Burden of Obesity in Italy.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Quantify the economic burden of obesity in Italy and explore, through an illustrative scenario-based approach, the potential budgetary implications for the Italian National Health Service (NHS) of full reimbursement of modern Obesity Management Medications (OMMs), including GLP-1 receptor agonists and dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists. Methods: Narrative review based on literature searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar from inception to September 2026 and covering the epidemiology and economic burden of obesity in Italy, the current AIFA reimbursement landscape, cost-effectiveness evidence for approved OMMs, and international reimbursement models. Evidence synthesized from cost-of-illness studies, clinical trials, health technology assessments, and economic modeling. Results: Obesity imposes an estimated €13 billion annual burden on Italy (direct costs €7.89 billion; indirect costs €5.45 billion). AIFA currently restricts reimbursement primarily to patients with obesity plus type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) via Nota 13, excluding the majority of individuals with obesity. Modern pharmacotherapies, including semaglutide 2.4 mg and tirzepatide, achieve 12-22% weight reduction with favorable cost-effectiveness ratios in several non-Italian economic evaluations, whereas Italian-specific analyses are lacking. In an illustrative scenario-based estimate derived from indirect modelling assumptions (not a validated decision-analytic, budget-impact, or cost-effectiveness model, and without formal sensitivity analysis), full reimbursement could avoid approximately €2-4 billion in obesity-related healthcare costs over 10 years (gross avoided costs; medication expenditure was not netted off and net savings were not demonstrated) through prevention of T2DM, cardiovascular disease (CVD), obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), and other obesity-related comorbidities. Conclusions: Full reimbursement of evidence-based Obesity Management Medications (OMMs) may offer long-term value for the Italian NHS, although reimbursement decisions require dedicated Italian cost-effectiveness and budget-impact analyses. Policy priorities should include expanding AIFA Nota 13 criteria, implementing outcomes-based risk-sharing agreements, and formally recognizing obesity as a chronic disease in Italian health policy.

papers.title: Twenty-Four-Hour Movement Behavior Compositions and Uncorrected Visual Acuity Among Chinese Junior High School Students: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study Using Optimal Time Zone Analysis.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Movement behaviors compete for a finite daily time budget. This study examined associations between 24-h movement composition and uncorrected visual acuity among Chinese junior high school students and explored model-derived candidate time allocations. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 865 students, split into derivation (n = 433) and internal validation (n = 432) samples. Robust regression modeled standardized log-transformed uncorrected visual acuity using isometric log-ratio (ilr) coordinates. The highest-predicted 5% of candidate compositions defined an exploratory region. Validation retained all 432 students; alternative search settings and bootstrap resampling assessed sensitivity. Results: The three ilr coordinates were jointly associated with the outcome (Wald χ2 = 28.433, df = 3, p < 0.001). Among 7488 candidates, 375 were selected. Marginal ranges were 190-360 min/day for light-intensity physical activity, 60-80 for moderate-to-vigorous physical activity, 510-800 for sedentary behavior, and 310-490 for sleep. Two validation participants fell within all four ranges. Each additional marginal range met was associated with a 0.053-point higher visual acuity score (95% confidence interval: 0.005-0.100; p = 0.031). The corresponding confidence intervals included zero with a 5-min grid and alternative selection fractions. Conclusions: These findings provide preliminary evidence to inform research on daily activity patterns and their associations with uncorrected visual acuity among Chinese junior high school students. The candidate allocations remain exploratory and sensitive to analytical settings. Further studies addressing clustering, confounding, and measurement limitations are needed before specific activity or sleep recommendations can be made.

papers.title: Measuring the Mind Through the Body: A Critical Integrative Narrative Review of Stress and Psychological Inference in Consumer Wearables.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Consumer wearables measure physiological and behavioural signals that may correlate with stress or affect, but physiological stress, subjective distress and psychiatric symptoms require different validation standards. This critical integrative narrative review examines which validation claims are supported and under which conditions. Methods: Structured literature searches were conducted from 9 April to 30 August 2026 in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, APA PsycINFO and IEEE Xplore, covering publications from January 2015 to 30 August 2026, with earlier foundational sources considered where pertinent. Recorded Boolean search strategies, narrative eligibility criteria and a descriptive evidence-appraisal framework guided a targeted integrative synthesis. As a narrative rather than systematic review, database hit counts and exclusion tallies were not recorded, and no PRISMA selection flow is asserted. Results: Selected laboratory and short-term field studies support stress detection under defined conditions, and personalised approaches are promising. Naturalistic associations vary with the target construct and comparator: in a study enrolling 781 students, analysed outcome samples differed (stress, n = 730; sleep, n = 709; tiredness, n = 781). Wearable-self-report sleep associations were stronger than those for tiredness, and Garmin stress was only weakly associated with self-reported stress (standardised β = 0.026, 95% CI 0.019-0.033; n = 730). Sensor-equity findings have different endpoints and do not establish disparities in HRV-based psychological scores. Conclusions: Wearable validity should be assessed against the exact physiological, psychological or clinical claim. Five proposed, claim-sensitive checkpoints operationalise recurrent gaps identified across the five analytic axes and are mapped to established V3/V3+ and COSMIN concepts; they have not been independently validated.

papers.title: Evaluation and Management of Central Sleep Apnea in Adults: A Comprehensive Review.
papers.abstract: Central sleep apnea (CSA) comprises a group of disorders characterized by recurrent re-duction or cessation of respiratory effort during sleep, resulting from diminished or absent central ventilatory drive. This narrative review presents current knowledge about the pathophysiology, diagnostics, classification, and treatment of adult CSA. Methods: The literature was chosen from peer-reviewed studies, clinical trials, guidelines, and systematic reviews on adult CSA with particular focus on CSA related to heart failure, opioids, high altitude, treatment-emergent CSA, positive airway pressure modes, pharmacological therapy, and phrenic nerve stimulation. Results: Current data suggest that the phenotype-directed approach with PSG, respiratory effort, comorbidity, and pharmacological history assessment allowed for the classification of CSA syndromes in relation to hyperventilation, hypoventilation, treatment-induced, and cause-dependent forms. CPAP, oxygen, BPAP-ST, ASV, acetazolamide, and transvenous phrenic nerve stimulators have different efficacy in certain CSA types with unclear data on the long-term cardiovascular outcomes, especially in patients with heart failure and exposure to opioids. Conclusions: Adult CSA management should be individualized according to mechanism, comorbidity profile, symptom burden, treatment safety, and measurable clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Multi-Type Clinical Interaction Modeling for Identifying Factors Associated with Cardiovascular Disease in Obstructive Sleep Apnea via an Interpretable Heterogeneous Graph Transformer.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a prevalent sleep disorder strongly associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD). The relationship between OSA and CVD is complex, involving multiple physiological and clinical factors. Identifying key contributors to cardiovascular risk in OSA patients is essential for early intervention, personalized treatment, and improved patient outcomes. Methods: We propose a heterogeneous graph learning model, RiskHGT, to identify influential clinical factors and interaction patterns associated with CVD in a cross-sectional analysis distinguishing OSA patients with and without prevalent CVD. By leveraging the advantages of heterogeneous graphs in modeling multi-relational medical data, RiskHGT captures intricate relationships among clinical factors and enables interpretation of the most influential factors associated with CVD in OSA patients. The model was trained and evaluated on two large-scale clinical sleep cohorts, the Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS) and the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA), with predictive performance assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC). Results: RiskHGT achieved superior predictive performance compared with baseline machine learning and graph-based models, reaching an AUROC of up to 0.94 and an AUPRC of up to 0.90. Fasting glucose, diastolic blood pressure, smoking status, and age were identified as the factors most strongly associated with CVD in OSA patients. Conclusions: RiskHGT provides interpretable, attention-based insights into clinical factors associated with CVD in patients with OSA. The framework may have potential for clinical use, but external and prospective validation is required before any clinical application.

papers.title: Dihydromyricetin Regulates Sleep and Protects Against Oxidative Stress in Drosophila melanogaster.
papers.abstract: Sleep homeostasis is essential for health, and sleep disturbances contribute to multi-organ failure mortality. Dihydromyricetin (DMY), a flavonoid from Ampelopsis grossedentata, possesses anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. Although DMY alleviates sleep-deprivation-induced cognitive deficits, its role in sleep regulation remains unclear. Here, we show that DMY increases sleep duration and modulates sleep fragmentation in young, aged, and short-sleep mutant Drosophila. Transcriptomic and genetic analyses reveal that DMY alters the expression of neurotransmitter-related genes, including VGAT and Trhn, suggesting potential involvement of GABAergic and serotonergic signaling. In paraquat-induced oxidative stress models, DMY boosts antioxidant gene expression, alleviates oxidative damage and intestinal apoptosis, restores stress-disrupted sleep, and extends lifespan. Together, our findings demonstrate that DMY improves sleep-associated parameters, potentially involving neurotransmitter-related signaling pathways while concurrently mitigating oxidative stress-induced damage, thereby promoting organismal health and suggesting its potential for preventing and treating sleep disorders and aging-related decline.

papers.title: Phagocytic NADPH Oxidase (NOX-2) as a Central Oxidative Effector in Experimental Models of Transportation-Noise-Induced Cardiovascular and Cerebral Disease.
papers.abstract: Transportation noise is an established cardiovascular risk factor. More than 112 million Europeans are chronically exposed above the thresholds of the Environmental Noise Directive, with approximately 73,000 premature deaths and 1.5 million disability-adjusted life years attributed annually. Large cohort studies demonstrate near-linear exposure-response relationships with ischaemic heart disease, myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure and type 2 diabetes, and more recently with dementia, Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson disease, independent of air pollution, detectable below guideline limits and stronger for night-time exposure. The noise reaction model attributes these effects to annoyance, sleep fragmentation and activation of the sympathetic nervous system and the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, converging on oxidative stress, inflammation and endothelial dysfunction. This review argues that the phagocytic NADPH oxidase NOX-2 (gp91phox) is a decisive oxidative effector within that cascade in experimental models of noise exposure. NOX-2 is upregulated in the vasculature and brain after aircraft noise exposure, is delivered to the vessel wall largely by infiltrating myelomonocytic cells, and drives superoxide formation, peroxynitrite generation, and uncoupling of endothelial and neuronal nitric oxide synthase. Genetic deletion of Nox2 prevents, essentially, the entire vascular phenotype and attenuates cerebral oxidative stress and neuroinflammation, whereas ablation of lysozyme M-positive myeloid cells reproduces the vascular but not cerebral protection. These causal data derive predominantly from short-term rodent aircraft-noise models and require further extrapolation in chronic human exposure settings. In line with this proposed mechanism of action, noise-mediated organ damage can be mitigated by pharmacological and lifestyle-associated anti-oxidant interventions that are also briefly summarised here.
